If, however, they share a common entrance or any other element that remains undivided, and the sale falls upon the seller's share in that common property, then pre-emption applies to it.

When undivided and divided property are sold together in a single transaction, the partner in the jointly held portion may claim the whole — both the common and the divided parts. He may not take one without the other, unless both parties agree to it.

If a buyer purchases the common share at an agreed price and the sale is concluded between him and the seller, and the seller then reduces part of that price so that the sale finally rests on the lesser amount actually received, the pre-emptor who subsequently comes forward may not demand to take the property at the original, higher price. He is entitled only to what was in fact paid, since the sale came to rest on that reduced sum.

If a seller sells the property at an agreed price and then returns some or all of that price to the buyer — whether as a gift or as charity — the pre-emptor who comes forward to exercise his right must pay the price upon which the sale was originally contracted. He may not deduct what the seller returned to the buyer, for that return was a stratagem designed to extinguish the pre-emption.

The same principle applies when the device runs the other way. Should the seller inflate the declared price and then hand the surplus back to the buyer, or should the buyer pay part of the sum as profit and part as price in order to circumvent the pre-emptor, what governs is the underlying contract and the true intention behind it. The sale is held to rest upon the whole price, or upon what was genuinely received. Gifts and charitable transfers used to disguise the real transaction do not defeat the pre-emptor's right.

If the price was inflated and the pre-emptor still wishes to proceed, he pays only what the buyer actually paid and receives everything the two parties genuinely agreed upon. This is established either by the buyer's own acknowledgment — made against his own interest — or by clear proof that the arrangement was a contrivance. If the pre-emptor merely alleges manipulation without proof, and the other party denies it, the most that can be required of the denying party is an oath in answer to the claim.

Such manipulation to defeat pre-emption is unlawful for both seller and buyer alike. It is a conspiracy to extinguish one of the established rights.

Where a sale has been concealed, the pre-emptor's right runs from the moment the sale comes to his knowledge, and remains open for one year — just as it does when the sale is open and known. Equally, if the *shafi* holds the right of pre-emption and the sale was conducted in secret, his claim may be pressed from the moment he learns of it, and that right remains available to him for one year, even if the sale was in fact publicly known and he was present when it took place.

If he allows the year to pass and only then claims he was never informed of the sale, his claim is not accepted, because the sale was a matter of common knowledge. The duty to claim does not arise until the sale has been concluded and finalized. Once it is concluded and finalized and the pre-emptor is bound to his claim, that obligation holds even if the seller has not yet received the price — and the pre-emptor may pay whichever of the two parties he chooses, whether the seller or the buyer.

If the pre-emptor proceeds against the buyer, the buyer's obligation extends only to delivering the property to him. The warranty for that property rests upon the original seller; no warranty falls upon the buyer when the pre-emptor proceeds against him, since the delivery traces back to the seller.

If the buyer has built upon the purchased property that is subject to pre-emption, or has sown it, that act counts as a completed taking of possession.

If a man claims to have purchased the property from someone who is absent, the pre-emptor may come forward, yet neither the sale nor the pre-emption is established against the absent party. The pre-emptor may not exercise his right until the sale is shown to be valid. Likewise, if a man claims to have purchased from someone present who denies the sale, the pre-emptor may not press his claim until the sale is validated — and his right of pre-emption then runs from the moment of that validation.

If a house is held as an endowment for particular named persons, and one of them builds within it and then dies — so that his portion passes to his heirs — and some of those heirs sell their inherited share, the right of pre-emption belongs to the remaining heirs. Whoever relinquished his pre-emption before the sale, and then comes forward after the sale has taken place, is free to press his claim or to leave it, since a relinquishment is not binding until after the sale has been concluded.

If the pre-emptor and the buyer disagree over the price, the buyer's word is accepted under oath that he purchased at the price he names, and that price is what the pre-emptor pays — unless clear evidence is established to the contrary. Equally, if the pre-emptor accepts the buyer's word, or the buyer swears and the pre-emptor pays him that sworn price, and it afterward emerges through evidence that the buyer in fact purchased for less, or the buyer himself admits as much, the pre-emptor may recover from him whatever was charged above the true price.

If the pre-emptor exercises his right and then exchanges the property and sells it onward, and afterward turns to the buyer demanding that the buyer pay him the price and return what was bought from him — making that the substance of his pre-emption claim — he is bound to carry it through. If he does not press the claim, nothing is required of him.

This represents, in its entirety, the position of the Ahl al-Bayt, may.

**On the preservation of oaths and covenants**

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "And guard your oaths" (Al-Maidah 89). And: "And those who are keepers of their trusts and their covenant" (Al-Muminun 8). And He said: "Fulfill the covenant of Allah when you have made a covenant, and do not break your oaths after their confirmation, when you have made Allah a surety over you" (Al-Nahl 91). And He said: "Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their own oaths for a small price will have no share in the Hereafter; Allah will not speak to them, nor look upon them on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and theirs is a painful punishment" (Al Imran 77).

The Messenger of Allah forbade swearing by any other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and said: "Whoever swears, let him swear by Allah; whoever swears by Allah, let him be truthful; and whoever has another swear to him by Allah, let him accept it; and whoever does not do so is no Muslim." He also said: "Three are those at whom Allah will not look on the Day of Resurrection, whom He will not purify, and for whom there is a painful punishment: a man who pledges allegiance to an imam for a portion of this world, so that if he is given it he keeps faith, and if he is not given it he withholds it; a man who has water beside the road and denies it to the traveler; and a man who swears after the afternoon prayer that he was offered such-and-such for his goods, so that another takes him at his word and accepts it, while he is lying."

Ali, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not hallow one who swears by His name falsely." It is also related from him that he said: "Beware the false oath, for it makes the merchandise sell but wipes away the blessing; and whoever swears a false oath has been audacious against Allah, so let him await His punishment." And he, the blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Whoever breaks his pledge of allegiance will meet Allah on the Day of Resurrection maimed" — meaning he will have no hand.

**On what is binding in oaths and what is not**

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "Allah will not take you to task for the thoughtless word in your oaths" (Al-Baqarah 225). Jafar ibn Muhammad, the blessings of Allah be upon him, said: Allah will not call you to account for the thoughtless word in your oaths. The thoughtlessness meant here is a man's saying "No, by Allah" and "Yes, by Allah" while his heart is not set upon the oath — that is, what a person utters in the ordinary flow of speech, swearing by Allah within it without any intention of swearing. This is confirmed by the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that follow: "Allah will not take you to task for the thoughtless word in your oaths, but He will take you to task for the oaths your hearts have deliberately bound" (Al-Maidah 89) — meaning what the swearer has resolved in his heart to swear upon.

Jafar ibn Muhammad, the blessings of Allah be upon him, made this plain. Of a man who declares, in the course of ordinary speech, "By Allah, I did not do it," concerning something he did in fact do — while his conscience is not fixed upon the oath — he said: "It is a lie he has told; let him seek Allah's forgiveness for it." He also said: "The oath is according to what the claimant administers it upon."

It is further related that he forbade equivocation in oaths. He held that if a man has been wronged, the oath is judged by the intention of the one who swears it; if he is the wrongdoer, it is judged by the intention of the one who administers it.

Equivocation is the use of likeness in speech: a man intends one thing but frames it in terms that suggest another, leading the listener to take the suggested meaning as the true one, while he conceals an altogether different intent. As for the People of the Book, they are made to swear by Allah and by whatever they hold in reverence within their own faith.

Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad, the blessings of Allah be upon him, commented on the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And remember your Lord when you forget" (Al-Kahf 24). The verse, he said, concerns the oath. If one says, "By Allah, I will surely do such-and-such," and forgets to make the exception, then upon remembering, one should say, "if Allah wills."

He then related that Ali, the blessings of Allah be upon him, reported that a company of Jews came to the Messenger of Allah and put a question to him. The Messenger replied, "Tomorrow I will tell you of it," and waited for revelation from Allah, Mighty and Majestic — yet he had not made the exception in his words. The revelation was withheld from him for forty days, after which these verses came down upon him: "And never say of anything, Indeed I will do that tomorrow, except that Allah wills; and remember your Lord when you forget" (Al-Kahf 23–24).

The masters of this tradition commanded that an oath include the exception — placing the will of Allah before the sworn word — and held this to be commendable. The Commander of the Believers, the blessings of Allah be upon him, said that whoever swears and then says "if Allah wills" incurs no perjury. Jafar ibn Muhammad, the blessings of Allah be upon him, said that if a man moves his tongue with the exception, the exception holds, even if he does not say it aloud. He also related that the Messenger of Allah said: a man's oath admits of an exception, and that exception stands when it is joined to the oath — when he swears and then says "if Allah wills" before his speech breaks off. By consensus, this is a permissible exception, and one who swears and excepts in this way does not fall into perjury.

Jafar ibn Muhammad, the blessings of Allah be upon him, said further that the exception remains permissible even after forty days. The ground for this is the case of the Messenger of Allah himself: revelation was withheld from him after his words to the Jews who questioned him — "Tomorrow I will tell you" — and when it came, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said, "And remember your Lord when you forget" (Al-Kahf 24). The exception arrived with that verse, forty days after the oath was spoken. A parallel report is transmitted from Ali, the Commander of the Believers, the blessings of Allah be upon him. And it is related from Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, the blessings of Allah be upon him, that he said: the exception is permissible even after a year.

The exception in an oath applies only to what the swearer himself swore he would or would not do. When a man is put under oath over a right claimed against him — when he swears to the claimant and makes an exception, whether silently or aloud — that exception counts for nothing. Such an oath rests on intentions, on the apparent words spoken, and on the intention of the one who administers it. If the swearer conceals something by which he means to escape the oath, or devises a trick within it, or equivocates, nothing of the obligation is lifted from him; the oath and the perjury both stand. He must discharge what he swore to the one to whom it is due, and repent thereafter and seek forgiveness. There is no expiation for perjury in such a case except that he carry out what he swore for the one entitled to it, and then turn in repentance and seek forgiveness.

No oath binds over what the swearer does not possess. A man who swears he will free a slave he does not own, or give away something not in his possession, has sworn nothing that holds. There is no oath by divorce, nor by manumission, nor by Hajj, nor by Umrah, nor by anything else among the forms sworn by other than Allah, Blessed and Exalted. The oath is by Allah alone, Mighty and Majestic.

> وَإِذْ أَسَرَّ ٱلنَّبِىُّ إِلَىٰ بَعْضِ أَزْوَجِهِۦ حَدِيثًۭا

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, the blessings of Allah be upon him, was asked about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:

> وَإِذْ أَسَرَّ ٱلنَّبِىُّ إِلَىٰ بَعْضِ أَزْوَجِهِۦ حَدِيثًۭا

"And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a certain matter" (Al-Tahrim 3), to the end of the verse.

The Master said that the Messenger of Allah had been alone with his bondwoman Mariyah the Copt at the very beginning of her arrival, before he had yet settled her in a house, when Aishah came upon him. She questioned him about it, and he, wishing to please her, swore that he would not return to Mariyah, forbade her to himself, and charged his wife to keep the matter secret. She did not keep it secret, but told it to Hafsah, and the two of them joined together against him. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down:

"O Prophet, why do you forbid yourself what Allah has made lawful for you?" (Al-Tahrim 1)

and commanded him to expiate the oath he had sworn (Al-Tahrim 5).

Allah did not make anything binding upon him through his act of forbidding to himself what was lawful; He rebuked him for it. Therefore, whoever forbids to himself what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made lawful for him, that thing is not thereby forbidden to him. It remains lawful for him, he may partake of it, and nothing is upon him. If he has also sworn an oath, he expiates that oath and partakes of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made lawful for him. The Messenger of Allah said: "Whoever swears an oath upon a matter and then sees that what is contrary to what he swore is better for him, let him do that which is better and expiate his oath."

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, the blessings of Allah be upon him, said that every oath sworn in disobedience counts for nothing — there is neither perjury nor expiation in it. Whoever swears that he will not do what is obligatory upon him, or that he will do what is permitted to him, and then refrains from what is forbidden and does what is obligatory, incurs neither perjury nor expiation. Whoever swears, in an act of obedience, that he will perform it, must fulfil what he swore; and if he does not, he expiates his oath.

**On Vows**

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "Indeed the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is camphor" (Al-Insan 5), up to His words, Mighty and Majestic: "They fulfill their vows and fear a Day whose evil is widespread" (Al-Insan 7). The Messenger of Allah forbade the vow made to other than Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and equally forbade any vow made in disobedience or in the severing of kinship.

edits.chapter_key: the body's portion: food, drink, and healing
edits.body_md:
The law draws a clear line between what may be eaten from a slaughtered animal and what must be left aside. Among the parts that are not eaten are the male glands, the penis, the female organ, and the inner flesh of the kidneys.

It is narrated from him (ع) that he said: "Nothing of the creatures of the sea is to be eaten except what is caught alive and has scales. As for what dies in the water before it is taken, or what has no scales, eating it is forbidden."

He forbade eating cheese made by Magians and polytheists when they introduce into it rennet (al-anfaha) drawn from carrion or from an animal over which the name of Allah was not pronounced. If the origin of the cheese is unknown, however, and there is no evidence that any such substance is in it, then eating it is permitted when it is sold in the market of the Muslims — just as one may eat the slaughtered meat sold there.

Everything whose eating is forbidden becomes permissible for the one in dire necessity, when nothing else can be found and life is at risk. The one compelled by need may eat of it until he is satisfied, if he so wishes.

Everything that nourishes — grains, green herbs, the produce of the earth, and all fruits that neither harm nor kill — is lawful to eat. The flesh of camels, cattle, sheep, and wild animals, together with their milk, is likewise lawful, with one exception: beasts of prey that possess fangs and seize and devour other animals. Nothing of such creatures is lawful to eat. All birds are lawful when properly slaughtered, except birds of prey that possess talons and seize and devour other birds; eating them is not lawful, nor is eating their eggs.

When an egg is found and its origin is unknown, it is examined. If its two ends differ — one pointed, one rounded — it may be eaten, for that is the egg of a creature whose flesh is lawful. If its two ends are alike, it is not eaten, for that is the egg of a creature whose flesh is not lawful.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted the eating of rabbit, but disliked the lizard (al-dabb), the hedgehog, and the other creeping things of the earth.

From Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) it is narrated that he permitted the use of vessels that had been touched by impurity or wine, provided they were washed and cleaned. Concerning food in which small creatures of the earth, flies, or other bloodless things happened to die, he held that this neither forbids the food nor renders it impure. Whoever is repelled by it may leave it; whoever wishes may eat. If, however, a creature possessing blood dies in the food, then the ruling differs: if the food is liquid, it is spoiled entirely; if it is solid, only what immediately surrounds the dead creature is spoiled. Once that portion has been removed and discarded, whoever wishes may eat the rest, and there is no harm in it.

**On the Etiquette of Drinking**

It is narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he forbade drinking in one continuous draft and commanded that one drink in sips, that the drinker name Allah at the first sip and praise Him when finished, and that he not breathe into the vessel. He should say "Bismillah" when beginning and "Alhamdulillah" when pausing.

Ali (ع) said: "I observed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drinking water more than once. He would breathe three times during the drink, taking the vessel away from his mouth at each breath, saying Bismillah when he began and Alhamdulillah when he paused."

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (ع) said: "Three breaths in a drink are better than one."

He forbade drinking from the mouth of a waterskin — that is, bending its opening back and drinking directly from it — on the grounds that doing so fouls the skin and risks a creature lurking unseen in the water slipping down the drinker's throat.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself drank both standing and sitting, yet he forbade lapping water directly from a river, a basin, a pond, or anything of that kind. Seeing a man do so, he said to him: "You lap as a beast laps. If you find no vessel, drink from your hand, for it is the best of your vessels."

He also forbade gulping water down, saying: "Suck the water as it is sucked, and do not gulp it down as a burden upon yourself, for that brings on disease of the liver (al-kubad)." Milk, however, he would gulp. Ali ibn al-Husayn (ع) was once observed gulping milk, and when he was asked, "Will you not take it in sips?" he replied: "Only the people of the Fire take it in sips." When he drank milk he would say: "O Allah, bless us in it and increase us from it." When he drank water he would say: "Praise be to Allah, who has given us fresh, sweet water by His mercy, and has not given us bitter, briny water on account of our sins."

It is narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad that he forbade drinking, or performing ablution, from the side of the handle (urwa) of the vessel.

**On What Is Permissible to Drink**

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ is reported to have said: "Water is the master of drinks in this world and the Hereafter." Any naturally occurring water, in which no human labor plays any part, is lawful and permitted to drink, so long as it has not been mixed with impurity and is neither harmful nor injurious. It is likewise permissible to drink the milk of every animal whose flesh is lawful to eat.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said of camel's milk: "It draws from every tree." And he said: "Cow's ghee is a cure, and its milk is medicine." A prophet once complained of a weakness he found in his body, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to him: "The finest meat is that taken with milk; eat them both, for I have placed strength in both of them." It is also said: "Meat and milk are the broth of the prophets."

He said: "Honey is a healing." Ali said: "No sick person was ever healed by the like of honey." And he said: "Can any of you not, when he falls ill, ask his wife to give him a dirham or two from her dowry, and buy honey with it, and drink it dissolved in rainwater?"

> وَنَزَّلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ مُّبَرَكًۭا

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says regarding the dowry: ﴿فَإِنْ طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ نَفْسًا فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا﴾, "If they willingly give up to you any part of it, then consume it in satisfaction and ease" (al-Nisa: 4). Regarding honey, He says: ﴿فِيهِ شِفَاءٌ لِلنَّاسِ﴾, "In it is healing for people" (al-Nahl: 69). And regarding rainwater, He says: ﴿وَنَزَّلْنَا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً مُبَارَكًا﴾, "And We sent down from the sky blessed water" (Qaf: 9).

Water mixed with honey, milk, or anything similar is lawful to drink, as are drinks made from dates, raisins, or other sweeteners, provided they have not fermented. The same applies to everything pressed from grape juice, dates, raisins, or lawful fruits and herbs: such juice is lawful to drink as long as it has not turned, whether taken pure or mixed with water, and buying it, selling it, and benefiting from it are equally lawful. Grape juice that has been cooked until it thickens, without turning, is likewise lawful to drink — pure or mixed with water — for as long as it remains unchanged.

It has been narrated of Ali that he used to supply the people with al-tila: grape juice boiled until it gains body, so that if left to stand it does not ferment but sets instead like honey. That preparation, and anything like it, is lawful to drink, pure or mixed with water, so long as it does not change.

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali was asked about drinking pressed juice. He said: "There is no harm in it. Drink from a clean vessel that has not been seasoned with wine, and drink it as long as a large quantity does not intoxicate. But if a large quantity intoxicates, then a small quantity of it is forbidden. Do not drink what has stood a long while, for after an hour, or after a night, the pleasure of wine departs and only its sin remains. So fear Allah and call yourselves to account."

The Shia of Ali were known by recognizable marks: piety, diligence, restraint, the shunning of sins great and small, and love for the friends of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. It has been narrated from Ali that he said: "We used to soak raisins or dates in water in a clean vessel for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He would drink it that day and the next; and if it had changed by the third day, he ordered it poured away." This is the lawful drink called nabidh — named for what is cast, that is, thrown, into the water: dates, raisins, or the like, which sweeten it when the water is brackish. But if it is left to ferment, so that it boils, intensifies, and throws up froth, then it is wine, and a large quantity of it is forbidden once it intoxicates.

**On What Is Forbidden to Drink**

> يَٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوٓا۟

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّمَا الْخَمْرُ وَالْمَيْسِرُ وَالْأَنْصَابُ وَالْأَزْلَامُ رِجْسٌ مِنْ عَمَلِ الشَّيْطَانِ فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾, "O you who believe, intoxicants, gambling, stone altars, and divining arrows are but an abomination of Satan's handiwork, so avoid it, that you may be successful" (al-Maidah: 90). By this He forbade wine, just as He forbade all things unlawful.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ is reported to have said: "Wine is forbidden; no one drinks it in this world and then drinks it in the Hereafter, in the sacred enclosure of holiness (hazirat al-quds)." He also said: "Allah has cursed wine: its presser, the one who has it pressed, its seller, its buyer, its drinker, the one who serves it, the one who consumes its price, the one who carries it, and the one to whom it is carried." And he said: "That which intoxicates in large quantity is forbidden even in a small quantity." He forbade treating illness with wine and intoxicants, and forbade giving them to children or animals, declaring that the sin falls upon whoever does so.

It is narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn that he said: "Intoxicating drink comes from five things: dates, raisins, wheat, barley, and honey — that is, besides grapes." From Muhammad ibn Ali, upon his forefathers be peace, it is narrated: "The one addicted to wine will meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, on the day he meets Him as one who worships an idol; and whoever drinks a single draft of it, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will not accept a prayer from him for forty nights."

From Jafar ibn Muhammad it is narrated: "Paradise is forbidden to three: the one addicted to wine, the worshipper of idols, and the enemy of the family of Muhammad." From Ali it is narrated: "Whoever drinks wine and dies within forty days of having drunk it meets Allah, Blessed and Exalted, as one who worships an idol." He also said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade every intoxicant from every drink, and whatever the Messenger of Allah has forbidden, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden. Every intoxicant is forbidden, and that which intoxicates in large quantity is forbidden even in a small quantity."

A man from the people of Kufa said to him: "May Allah set you right — the jurists of our land say that only wine made from grapes is forbidden."

He replied: "O Sheikh, I do not know what the jurists of your land say. My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: that which intoxicates in large quantity is forbidden even in a small quantity."

Jafar ibn Muhammad then said: "Taqiyya is my religion and the religion of my forefathers in everything except three matters:

- the prohibition of intoxicants
- the removing of the two leather socks at ablution
- the saying aloud of Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim, meaning that it be recited aloud in the prayer"

Jafar ibn Muhammad said: "One must not treat illness with wine or intoxicants, nor may women use such things to dress their hair, for my father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, that Ali said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has placed no cure in any impurity that He has forbidden."

He was also asked about drinking al-fuqqa, and when the questioner had described its nature, he said: "It is forbidden; do not drink it."

Concerning seasoned vessels, he said that wine was not forbidden on account of such vessels, but that he had forbidden the intoxicant in small quantity and large alike; he disapproved of the seasoned vessels only because they alter the drinks.

---

**On What Makes Medicine Beneficial**

What follows is drawn from what has come down from the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), concerning medicine — the treatments and remedies they permitted and those they forbade — all of which belongs to the domain of the lawful and the unlawful. One who doubts what has come from them may well deny it upon hearing it; and if he applies it without true belief, he will find no benefit in it and so cast it aside. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, brings benefit through it only to those who affirm them and submit to their command, who receive what has come from them with acceptance — not to one who takes it as a mere trial, without belief, without intention, and without conviction.

What confirms this is the report narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad. Muhammad ibn Khalid, the governor of Medina, was recovering from an illness and complained, before a gathering of people, of a pain in his abdomen. Jafar ibn Muhammad said to him: "Shall I not tell you a hadith my father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: "Yes." Jafar said: "Abu Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn told me, from his father, from his grandfather, that a man complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of a pain he felt in his abdomen. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: Take a drink of honey and cast into it three grains of black seed (shuniz), or five, or seven, and you will be cured by the leave of Allah. He did so and was cured. So take this yourself."

A man of Medina who was present in the gathering objected and said: "O Abu Abd Allah, the hadith is sound, and we have heard it, but we tried it and gained no benefit from it."

At that, Abu Abd Allah (ع) grew very angry and said: "Allah brings benefit through this only to those who believe in Him and affirm His Messenger (ع) — the Muslims who submit to his command and receive it from him with acceptance. As for the hypocrites who doubt it and do not affirm him, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will not benefit them by it. Perhaps you are a hypocrite, and you took it without affirming the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and so you were denied its benefit."

The man fell silent, overcome with shame, and bowed his head. All who were present in the gathering affirmed the truth of Abu Abd Allah's words.

As for those who have used these remedies with sincere intention and certainty, the benefit they have received cannot be reckoned. Whoever turns to anything reported in these chapters — from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — seeking treatment and cure, ought to approach it with intention, sincerity, and certainty, for it will benefit him, if Allah wills. If doubt over it has entered his heart, he should not treat himself with its like; and if he inclines instead toward the word of the physicians where they have spoken against it, he will gain no benefit from it.

It is Allah who grants the success of affirming His friends, submitting to their command, and receiving and accepting from them, to those servants whom He is pleased with and chooses for His guardianship.

**On Seeking Healing Through Acts of Righteousness**

The Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ have narrated that he said: "In the black seed (al-habba al-sawda) is a cure for every disease except al-sam" — that is, death. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali conveyed this hadith to some of his companions, and it delighted them. They said: "O son of the Messenger of Allah, what an easy remedy this is — one that heals every disease but death!" He said: "Yes. Shall I not tell you of something easier still, one in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ excluded neither death nor anything else?" They said: "What is it, O son of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: "Supplication, for it turns back the decree even after it has been firmly sealed." He then joined all his fingers together, bringing the two little fingers side by side, to depict the firm sealing of the decree.

It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ noticed the absence of a man from among the Ansar. When the man came to him some time later, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked: "What has kept you from us?" The man replied: "Sickness and poverty, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shall I not teach you words to call upon Allah with, by which Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will lift that from you?" The man said: "Yes, by my father and my mother, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Say: There is no power and no strength except through Allah; I place my trust in the Living who does not die. Praise be to Allah, who has taken no son, who has no partner in His dominion, and who has no protector from humiliation; and magnify Him greatly."

It is also narrated from Ali that he said: "I complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of a forgetfulness that had come over me, on account of which much of the Quran was slipping away from me. He said to me: O Ali, I will teach you words that will drive that from you and fix the Quran firmly in your heart. Say: O Allah, have mercy on me through the forsaking of disobedience to You for as long as You keep me alive; have mercy on me by sparing me what does not concern me; grant me good discernment in what pleases You with me; bind my heart to the keeping of Your Book as You taught it to me; and grant that I recite it in the manner that pleases You."

Among the words he taught for the firm holding of revelation was this: by Your Book give light to my sight, release my tongue, open my chest with it, employ my body in it, and grant me strength through it, for none can grant strength in it but You. He said: I prayed with those words, and Allah established the Quran firmly in my chest.

It was narrated from him that he said: If one of you sets before him a vessel containing food or drink and fears that something in it may harm him, let him name Allah over it and take from it, for nothing harms alongside the name of Allah.

It was narrated from Abu Abd-Allah, (ع), that a man among his companions complained to him of a corruption he found in his stomach, saying that he could eat no food without it harming and distressing him. He said to him: Say the name of Allah over every food you eat, and over every variety of it as you eat it, and it will not harm you. The man did so and was cured.

It was also narrated from him that a man among his companions was struck with a whiteness between his eyes and complained of it, for the affliction had taken hold of him and caused him grief. The Master said to him: Make supplication while you are in prostration. The man said: O son of the Messenger of Allah, teach me the words to pray with. He said: Say: O Allah, O Most Merciful, O Compassionate, O Hearer of prayers, O Giver of good things, grant me the good of the Hereafter and of this world, turn away from me the evil of them both, and remove from me this affliction that is between my eyes, for it has grieved and saddened me. The man did so and was healed.

It was narrated from him that he said: Be eager for charity and give it early in the day, for there is no believer who gives a charity sincerely, desiring by it what is with Allah, except that Allah wards off from him the evil of what descends from the sky on that day and shields him from it. Then he said: And do not think little of the prayers of the poor for the sick among you, for they are answered on your behalf, though they may not be answered for the poor themselves.

Ismail ibn Ali entered Medina while ill, and Abu Abd-Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad came to visit him. Seeing his condition, he said: Call for a basket, fill it with wheat, and set it before you. Then instruct your servants that when a beggar comes, they bring him in to you — and hand him some of that wheat with your own hand, and ask him to pray to Allah for you.

Ismail said: Shall I not rather give them dirhams and dinars?

Abu Abd-Allah said: Do what I have commanded you.

He did so, and was granted health.

It was narrated from Abu Abd-Allah that he said: Three things drive away forgetfulness and bring on remembrance:

- reciting the Quran
- using the siwak
- fasting

It was narrated from him that a man among his companions complained of being heavily overtaken by worry and grief. He said: When anything of that befalls you, pass your hand over the place of your prostration, then draw your hand across your face — from the left side of your cheek, across your forehead, to the right side of your cheek — then say: In the name of Allah, there is no god but He, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, He is the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. O Allah, remove from me worry and grief. Let him do this three times.

It was narrated from him that whoever says, thirty times each day, the following words — *In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful; praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds; and blessed be Allah, the best of creators; and there is no power and no strength except through Allah, the Most High, the Most Great* — Allah will ward off from him ninety-nine kinds of affliction, the least of which is madness.

---

**Mention of bearing illness with patience for its reward**

The narration from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah reports that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, said: "The groaning of a sick man, if he is patient and counts it for reward, is recorded for him as good deeds. But if it is in panic, he is called one given to panic, and there is no reward for him."

The full treatment of this matter — and of the reward that illness carries for one who is patient and counts it for reward — belongs among the chapters on funerals.

It is also narrated from them that a woman came to the Messenger of Allah with a son of hers who was afflicted in his mind. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah for this son of mine that He may heal him."

He said: "As you wish. If you wish, I will pray to Allah for him and He will heal him; and if you wish, I will leave him, and there will be no reckoning or punishment upon him."

She said: "Then leave him, O Messenger of Allah" — and may Allah's prayers and —

---

**Mention of seeking refuge and the ruqyah**

The Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah have transmitted that he would seat al-Hasan and al-Husayn upon his thighs and seek refuge for them, saying: "I seek refuge for you both in the perfect words of Allah from every devil and every crawling thing, and from every envious eye." He would then add: "Thus did my father Ibrahim (ع) seek refuge for his two sons Ismail and Ishaq".

It was narrated that Labid ibn al-Asam the Jew and the Jewish woman Umm Abd-Allah worked sorcery against the Prophet by tying eleven knots in a cord of red and yellow threads, placing it inside the sheath of a date-palm, and lowering it into one of the steps of a well in Medina. As a result, the Messenger of Allah and his family were left unable to hear, to see, to stand, to speak, to eat, or to drink.

Then Jibril (ع) descended with the two chapters of refuge and said to him that Labid ibn al-Asam and the Jewish woman Umm Abd-Allah had worked sorcery against him. Jibril told him where the sorcery lay and recited over him: *In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of the Falaq*, and *Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind*, to the end of the two chapters.

As the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his family recited, one knot was loosened and he sat up; he recited again and another knot was loosened. This continued until he had recited eleven times, all eleven knots were loosened, and the Prophet ﷺ and his family sat up, free of the sorcery's hold. He then ordered Ali, who retrieved the sorcery from the well in which it had been placed. The Prophet summoned Labid and Umm Abd-Allah and said: "What moved you to do what you have done?" Then he said to Labid: "May Allah not bring you out of this world safe and sound." Labid was a man of wealth and great means.

Labid met his end not long after. He passed by a boy who wore an earring worth a dinar, snatched it, and tore the boy's ear in the taking. His hand was cut off and cauterized for the crime, yet the bleeding would not stop, and he bled until he died.

Ali said: "I fell gravely ill, so that I could find no rest upon my bed, and the Prophet and his family came to visit me. He said to me: 'O Ali, the most sorely tried of people in this world are the prophets, then those who come after them, then those who come after them. Rejoice, for this is your share of the chastisement of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, together with the reward laid up for you.' Then he said to me: 'Would you like Allah to lift from you what afflicts you?' I said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Say: O Allah, have mercy upon my thin skin and my fragile bone, and I seek refuge in You from the surge of the burning. O Umm Maldam, if you have believed in Allah, then do not eat flesh, do not drink blood, and do not boil over upon the mouth; depart instead to one who claims that there is another god alongside Allah. And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger.' I said it, and I was healed at that very hour."

Jafar ibn Muhammad said: "I never turned to it in distress but that I found it answered; and they used to teach it even to women and children."

It was narrated from Ali that the Messenger of Allah, and his family, granted license for ruqyah by the Book of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and by whatever is known of His remembrance and His names. He said that these incantations are among what Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon him, held as authority over the jinn.

It was also narrated from him that the Messenger of Allah, and his family, said: There is no ruqyah except in three things: a festering wound, an evil eye, or blood. Some hold that ruqyah is for the sting of the scorpion and the sting of the wasp, but that is a mistake. The hummah is the venom present in such creatures — the scorpion, the serpent, and others like them — for the hummah is itself a venomous creature, while the scorpion's sting is merely a needle.

It was narrated of the Messenger of Allah, and his family, that he sent out a company of men, and they passed by an Arab tribe whose chief had been stung. The tribesmen asked whether anyone among the company could perform a ruqyah. One of them recited over the chief the Opening of the Book, and the man was cured. When the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, was told of this, he approved it. One of his wives likewise performed a ruqyah with the two chapters of refuge, and he approved that as well, saying to her: And how did you know that it is a ruqyah?

The Master said, peace be upon him and his family: *There is no contagion, no ill omen from birds, and no ham; but the evil eye is real and the good omen is real.* He also said, peace be upon him and his family: *When one of you looks upon a person, or a beast, or anything pleasing that delights him, let him say: I have believed in Allah; may Allah bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad — then his eye will not harm what he looked upon.* It is narrated that when an evil eye struck him, or a headache came upon him, he would spread out his two hands, recite into them the Opening of the Book and the two chapters of refuge, then wipe his face with them, and whatever he had been feeling would depart.

He and his family also forbade:

- Sorcery
- Soothsaying
- Amulets
- Tiwalah

Amulets are objects hung upon a person that bear something other than the names of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. Tiwalah is what women prepare in order to draw their husbands' love toward them. Jafar ibn Muhammad said: *There is no harm in a charm that is hung if it contains something of the Quran.*

A man once complained to Abu Abd-Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad of a pain he had found in himself. The Master said: "Say 'In the name of Allah' and wipe over the place, then say: 'I seek refuge in the might of Allah, I seek refuge in the power of Allah, I seek refuge in the majesty of Allah, I seek refuge in the greatness of Allah, I seek refuge in all the bounds of Allah, I seek refuge in the names of Allah, and I seek refuge in the names of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family, from the evil of what I find.' Let him say this seven times." The man said: "I said it, and what I had been suffering left me."

It was narrated from him and his family that he said: "When you wish to seek refuge, clasp your two palms together and recite into them the Opening of the Book and *Say, He is Allah, One* three times, then lay them upon the place of pain. Clasp them again, recite into them the Opening of the Book and *Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of the Falaq* three times, and lay them upon the pain a second time. Clasp them once more, recite into them the Opening of the Book and *Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind* three times, and lay them upon the pain. Three times in all."

It was narrated from Ali that he said: whoever is ill-tempered, let the call to prayer be given in his ear. Abu Abd-Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad said of the sick man who has a ruqyah performed for him: there is no harm in it, so long as the ruqyah is by something known. It was narrated from Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali that he said: "When you wish to perform a ruqyah upon a wound, against pain, or blood, or what is feared for it, place your hand upon the wound and say: *In the name of Allah I perform your ruqyah; in the name of Allah the Greatest, against iron and stone, and the dark fang and the running of sweat, so let it not deceive, and against the eye, so let it not keep vigil.* Repeat it three times."

---

**Mention of treatment and medicine:**

The narration from the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt records that the Messenger of Allah, and his family, was asked whether the sick should be treated and given remedies. He said: "Yes. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has sent down no disease without sending down a remedy with it, so seek treatment — except for the *sam*, which is death, for it has no cure."

A group of the Ansar brought him a question about one of their number who was suffering from a stomach complaint, and about a Jewish physician who treated such conditions by opening the abdomen. The Messenger of Allah, and his family, was reluctant and withheld his permission. They returned to him two or three times, and each time he refused, until at last he said to them: "Do as you wish." The Jewish physician was summoned. He opened the man's abdomen, removed a great deal of foul matter, washed and stitched it closed, and administered treatment — and the man recovered. When the Messenger of Allah, and his family, was told of this, he said: "He who created the disease has appointed for it a remedy; and the best of remedies are cupping, phlebotomy, and the black seed — which is the shuneez." The Messenger of Allah, and his family, also forbade imposing strict diets upon the sick.

He looked at Salman, who was eating dates while suffering from sore eyes, and said: "O Salman, you eat dates while your eyes are afflicted?"

Salman replied: "O Messenger of Allah, it is only my right eye that is sore, and I am chewing with my left teeth."

The Messenger of Allah smiled and did not stop him.

It was also narrated from him and his family that skipping the evening meal is a cause of weakness in old age. He said, and his family, that the sick should not be forced to eat, for Allah the Mighty and Majestic feeds them and gives them drink. It was narrated from him and his family that there is no harm in an enema, were it not that it enlarges the belly. He said, and his family: when blood becomes excessive in one of you, let him draw it off, even with a small blade — meaning when the blood overcomes him. He said, and his family: cupping of the head is a cure for every disease, and remedy lies in four things:

- Cupping
- The enema
- The depilatory
- Vomiting

Ali said: the Messenger of Allah was never seized by fever but that he turned to cupping. He used to say: "When blood becomes excessive in one of you, let him be cupped on whatever day it may be, and let him recite Ayat al-Kursi, seek the forgiveness of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and send blessings upon the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family. Do not hold certain days to be against you, lest they be set against you; be cupped on whichever of them you wish; and let him name Allah over the cupping vessel."

Among the narrated traditions concerning the body and its remedies is the matter of cupping: cupping of the head brings relief, and cupping of the upper back — the kahil — is beneficial. Fever, being from the heat of Hell, is to be cooled with water; whenever the Messenger of Allah and his family was seized with fever, he would call for water and place his hand in it.

Al-Hasan and al-Husayn once fell ill with fever, and Fatima came to the Messenger of Allah seeking help and refuge. She said, "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah for your son that He heal him, for he is gravely ill." The Messenger of Allah and his family rose, came to the boy, sat at his head, and found him in a heavy state. He said, "O Fatima, it is Allah the Almighty who bestowed him upon you, and He is able to heal him." Then Jibril came to him and said, "O Muhammad, Allah the Almighty has not sent down upon you a sura of the Quran that does not contain a fa — and every fa is an affliction, an afa — save al-Hamd, for there is no fa in it. So call for a cup of water, recite al-Hamd over it forty times, then pour it over him, and Allah the Almighty will heal him." The Messenger of Allah and his family did so, and it was as though the boy had been loosed from a tether.

It is narrated that he was asked about cauterisation, and he forbade it. Jafar ibn Muhammad said, "There is no objection to cauterisation. What was forbidden concerns that which is feared to cause death or that which disfigures the body. As for what one hopes will bring a cure, there is nothing wrong with it."

The Messenger of Allah and his family used to command applying kohl with ithmid before sleep, and he would say, "Apply kohl an odd number of times." He also said, "Use ithmid, for it makes the lashes grow, removes the motes from the eye, and clears the sight." He said and his family, "Al-Ajwa is from Paradise, and in it is a cure for poison." Some of the Ahl al-Bayt described its preparation as follows:

- Take Ajwa dates and remove their stones.
- Pound them thoroughly, then knead them with aged cow's ghee.
- Set the mixture aside; when someone who has taken poison is in need of it, he eats it, and it benefits him.

It is narrated that a scorpion stung the Messenger of Allah and his family. He struck it down and said, "May Allah curse you, for you spare neither believer nor disbeliever from your sting." He then called for salt, placed it upon the site of the sting, and pressed it with his thumb until it dissolved. He said, "If people knew what is in salt, they would have no need of any antidote alongside it."

It is narrated that he said, "Whoever eats twenty-one seedless raisins each morning on an empty stomach will not fall ill except with the illness in which he dies." And, "Whoever eats seven dates at his bedtime will be spared colic, and the worms in his belly will be killed." He said to Jafar ibn Abi Talib, "Eat quince, for it strengthens the heart and emboldens the coward."

He said, "Honey is a healing." Jafar ibn Muhammad said that Allah the Almighty has mentioned it in His Book, where He said of it, "فِيهِ شِفَآءٌۭ لِّلنَّاسِ," that is, "In it is a healing for people." He said ((ع) and his family), "Beware of al-shabram, for it is hot; and you must take senna, so treat yourselves with it, for if anything could repel death, senna would repel it. And treat yourselves with fenugreek, for if my nation knew what it holds for them, they would treat themselves with it even were it to cost its weight in gold." He forbade ((ع) and his family) the eating of clay and charcoal, and said that Allah the Almighty created Adam from clay and therefore forbade the eating of clay to his descendants. "Whoever eats clay has aided in his own harm, and whoever persists in eating clay until he dies of it, I will not pray over him." Jafar ibn Muhammad said that the eating of clay breeds hypocrisy.

The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) said that eating fresh, soft fish dissolves the body, and that one should not make a habit of it. When he ate fish, he would say, "O Allah, bless it for us and give us in its place what is better than it." Jafar ibn Muhammad said, "Whoever eats fish, let him eat dates afterward, for that removes its harm." The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) also forbade drinking al-hamim. Al-hamim is the rain that falls during the worst of the summer heat; it is also hot water, and more broadly any rainwater that falls in intense heat and runs along the ground until it grows hot and harmful. His prohibition was for that reason alone — not because al-hamim is unlawful or impure, but because the harm it causes made it blameworthy.

It is narrated from him that he said, "Whoever is a physician, or undertakes treatment — Arab or non-Arab — let him not treat anyone until he has obtained from him a written release, witnessed by witnesses. Let him fear Allah the Almighty, strive diligently, and counsel sincerely." By the release, he meant that the physician must be learned in medicine and must not treat people from a position of ignorance; for if he does, he bears liability for whatever harm results.

It is narrated from him that he used to say, "Whoever desires to endure — though there is no enduring — let him lighten his burden, keep to his sandals, take his morning meal early, draw his evening meal near, and lessen intercourse." He was asked, "O Commander of the Faithful, what is the lightening of the burden?" He replied, "It is debt."

The Master said, "The truffle is from the manna, and its water is a cure for the eye." Some of the Ahl al-Bayt described its preparation: a truffle is washed until clean, its water squeezed into a vessel, and a fire kindled beneath it until the liquid thickens; musk is then added, and the preparation is applied as kohl for all ailments of the eye. When its moisture dries, it is moistened with rainwater and applied as kohl once more. It is also narrated from Ali that he said, "Nothing restores the woman in childbirth like eating fresh, moist dates. Allah the Almighty fed Maryam fresh dates in her childbirth." He said, "Eat the pomegranate with its pith, for it is a tanner for the stomach. And you must eat apples, for they cleanse the stomach."

It is narrated from him and his family that the Messenger of Allah said, "Celery is the herb of the prophets, and there is no leaf of endive but that upon it is water from Paradise. You must take the gourd, for it strengthens the heart and the mind." He once trod upon scorching ground and it burned him, so he stepped onto purslane — the herb known as the foolish herb — and the heat of the ground subsided for him. He blessed it, and thereafter he ate it regularly and was fond of it. Ali said, "The sick are healed by nothing like the drinking of honey."

Jafar ibn Muhammad was asked about a man who seeks treatment from a Jew or a Christian. He said, "There is nothing wrong with that, for healing is in the hand of Allah the Almighty." He was also asked whether a woman who has a disease, a fracture, or a wound in a place not proper to be looked upon may uncover it to a male physician. He said, "There is nothing wrong with that when she is compelled to it." He was further asked about a man who treats people with medicine and charges a fee for doing so, and he said, "There is nothing wrong with it."

It is narrated from him that he said, "If people were moderate in their food and drink, their bodies would remain sound." He said, "Abandoning the evening meal is the ruin of the body." He said, "Allah the Almighty says, وَلَهُمْ رِزْقُهُمْ فِيهَا بُكْرَةًۭ وَعَشِيًّۭا — that is, and they shall have their provision therein, morning and evening." A man complained to him of pains and indigestion, and he said, "Take your midday meal and your evening meal, and eat nothing between them, for that is the corruption of the body." He said, "Abandoning the evening meal diminishes a strength that does not return," and, "Let not the aged man abandon the evening meal, even if it be only a morsel." He said, "Eating meat with milk makes the flesh grow and strengthens the bone." And he said, "A prophet among the prophets complained to Allah the Almighty of his few children, so He commanded him to eat meat with eggs."

It is narrated from him and his family that the Messenger of Allah and his family counseled Ali, saying, "O Ali, sleep upon your back, for it slims the belly. Drink water by sipping, for thereby your food is made wholesome. Wear a ring, and apply kohl an odd number of times, for it will brighten your sight. Anoint yourself every other day, in keeping with the Sunnah of your Prophet. Renew your sandals, for they are the anklets of a man, and turbans are the crowns of the Arabs. When you cook a pot, make its broth plentiful, for if your neighbors do not receive some of its meat, they will receive some of its broth. Wear a ring of ruby and carnelian, for it is fortunate and blessed; whenever a man looks at his face within it, it increases him in light, and the prayer offered wearing it is worth seventy prayers. Wear the ring upon your right hand, for that is the practice of the Messengers, and whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me. Do not wear a ring upon the left, nor of anything but ruby and carnelian."

It is narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad that one of his companions came to him complaining of pain in his loin. He said to the man, "Take what falls from the table during a meal, gather it up, and eat it." The man said, "I did so, and I was healed." Jafar ibn Muhammad then said, "Eat of the food that falls from the table, for in it is a healing, by the leave of Allah the Almighty, for whoever seeks healing by it — that is, for every disease."

A man once looked at apples in the hands of Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad, and he said to him, "The apple cools the heat and quenches it, and removes the fever."

He spoke of vinegar and said, "It firms the mouth and kills the worms of the belly."

He said, "Rice sawiq, when it is parched and ground, binds the belly; if part of it is made into sawiq and part into a gruel, it binds the belly likewise. Sawiq makes the flesh grow and strengthens the bone, and it benefits the feverish when it is moistened and washed three times. Take sawiq dry on an empty stomach, for it dispels phlegm and bile."

It is also narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn that he permitted treatment with the milk of she-asses, and that if one finds the milk of the wild ass, that is better.

edits.chapter_key: what we wear: dress, adornment, and fragrance
edits.body_md:
Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said: "Dress and adorn yourselves with what is lawful, for Allah, mighty and exalted, loves beauty." It is narrated that he went out one cold day wearing a fur cloak of yellow khazz and a yellow khazz mantle. When he saw the people staring at him, he said: "There was a prophet, the son of a prophet, the son of a prophet, the son of a prophet" — meaning Yusuf (ع) — "who wore robes of brocade fastened with gold and sat upon his throne to judge among the people."

Ali ibn al-Husayn (ع) used to wear in summer two garments bought for five hundred dirhams each, and in winter he wore khazz. Jafar ibn Muhammad was asked about a man who acquires many garments to adorn himself, keeping some in reserve to protect the others, and whether this constitutes excess. He said: "No, that is not extravagance. Allah, mighty and exalted, says: ﴿لِيُنفِقْ ذُو سَعَةٍ مِّن سَعَتِهِ﴾ Let the one who has abundance spend out of his abundance." (Al-Talaq: 7)

> قُلْ مَنْ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَخْرَجَ لِعِبَادِهِۦ وَٱلطَّيِّبَتِ مِنَ ٱلرِّزْقِ

Sufyan al-Thawri came in upon him and saw that he was wearing fine garments. He said: "O son of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, you tell us that Ali, (ع), used to wear coarse cloth and rough fabric, yet here you are dressed in al-Quhi and al-Muwri." He answered: "Woe to you, Sufyan. Ali lived in a time of hardship and scarcity, but Allah, mighty and exalted, has widened our means, and it is fitting for the one upon whom Allah has bestowed abundance that the trace of that bounty be seen upon him."

Ali ibn al-Husayn used to have a khazz mantle bought for him for fifty dinars, which he would wear through the winter, entering the mosque and praying in it. When summer came he would order that it be given away as charity on his behalf, and he would command that two garments of the Egyptian sort be bought for him, which would be readied and which he would wear in the summer, wearing between these the fine and the plain alike. When this was remarked upon to him, he would recite the words of Allah, mighty and exalted: ﴿قُلْ مَنْ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي أَخْرَجَ لِعِبَادِهِ وَالطَّيِّبَاتِ مِنَ الرِّزْقِ﴾ "Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants, and the good things of sustenance?" (Al-Araf: 32)

Ali once looked upon a group of people wearing wool and hair garments, and said to them: "Wear cotton, for that was the clothing of the Messenger of Allah — the best he could find — and it is our dress. He wore neither wool nor hair, so do not wear them except out of need, or when nothing else can be found. Allah, mighty and exalted, is beautiful and loves beauty, and He loves to see the trace of His blessing upon His servant."

It is narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad that he performed the Hajj, entering ihram in two fine garments. While he was making tawaf in them, a man tugged at the edge of his cloak. He turned and found it was Abbad al-Basri, who said to him: "O Abu Abdullah, you wear garments such as these, in a place such as this — knowing where you stand in relation to Ali, and knowing what his clothing was like?" He replied, (ع): "Woe to you, Abbad. Ali lived in a time when what he wore suited it. Were I to wear his dress today, people would say: this man is a pretender, like Abbad al-Basri." Abbad was already known for ostentation. He fell silent, covered in shame, while those around him exchanged glances at his expense.

It is also narrated from him that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: "Wear fine turbans, for they are the crowns of the Arabs."

It is further narrated from Abu Jafar Muhammad (ع) that some of his companions once entered his room and found it richly appointed — furnished with cushions, embroidered coverings, armrests, and bedding. On a later visit they found him in a room with nothing but a reed mat. They said to him: "May we be your ransom — what is this room?" He said: "This is my room. The room you saw before belongs to the women. Let me tell you something my father told me. He said: Some people once came in upon al-Husayn and found his dwelling spread with carpets, rugs, and many furnishings. They said: O son of the Messenger of Allah, we see in your house things that were not in the house of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family. He said: We marry women and give them their dowries, with which they furnish and prepare their homes."

As for clothing — whether fine or plain — wearing it, spreading it out, and wrapping oneself in it are all permissible, and nothing in this is disliked. Whoever chooses the plain out of humility, though finer clothing was within reach, has done nothing wrong. Whoever chooses the fine, finding it accessible and within his means, that too is permissible — indeed it is recommended, as a display of the grace of Allah, mighty and exalted. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, wore both the fine and the plain, whatever he chose for himself and whatever others clothed him in.

The Imams (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) are reported to have taught that clothing made from whatever the earth produces — wearing it, spreading it, wrapping oneself in it, praying in it and upon it — is lawful. Likewise, the skin, wool, hair, and fur of any animal whose flesh is permissible to eat are lawful and permitted, provided the animal was properly slaughtered. As for the wool, hair, fur, and skin of an animal that died without proper slaughter, wrapping oneself in such material, spreading it, and making use of it is permitted, as already noted — just as use is permitted of things that have been touched by impurities — with one exception: one may not pray in any of it, just as one does not pray in an impure garment.

> وَأَعِدُّوا۟ لَهُم مَّا ٱسْتَطَعْتُم مِّن قُوَّةٍۢ وَمِن رِّبَاطِ ٱلْخَيْلِ تُرْهِبُونَ بِهِۦ عَدُوَّ

The Imams disliked for a man to wear pure silk, though they permitted what was woven together with other material grown from the earth. It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, permitted it to certain people and allowed that one display and adorn oneself with it before the enemy, so that they might recognize the strength of the Muslims — in keeping with the words of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿وَأَعِدُّوا لَهُم مَّا اسْتَطَعْتُم مِّن قُوَّةٍ وَمِن رِّبَاطِ الْخَيْلِ تُرْهِبُونَ بِهِ عَدُوَّ اللَّهِ﴾ "And prepare against them whatever force you are able, and steeds of war, by which you strike fear into the enemy of Allah." (Al-Anfal: 60)

The Imams would themselves wear silk in this manner — woven with other materials and lined with what the earth grows — displaying it before the enemies of Allah, and they permitted it to whoever would display it in the same way. The world and all it contains ranked among the most trifling of things in their sight, yet they showed of it what they showed as a preparation for the strength of Islam and the Muslims, and as a display before those who set themselves against them and made themselves their enemies among all people.

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, loved white garments above all others, and would say: "It is the best of your clothing, so wear it, and shroud your dead in it." No dye, however, renders a garment forbidden to wear. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, and the Imams of his house wore dyed cloth, though they preferred certain dyes over others. It is narrated from Ali that he said: "Saffron is ours, and safflower yellow is for the Banu Umayyah." Jafar ibn Muhammad disliked a deep, heavily saturated red, saying: "It is the garb of Qarun and the dye of the Banu Umayyah." He himself wore safflower that was not intense in color.

It is narrated that Ali went out one day to the people of Kufa, walking from the palace to the open ground of al-Rahba. He wore a yellow waist-wrapper and a black khamisa, sandals on his feet, and in his hand an anaza — a staff upon which he leaned.

It is narrated of Jafar ibn Muhammad that he entered ihram in a green cloak, and of Ali ibn al-Husayn that he was seen wearing a black overgarment with a blue border. Yet the Imams (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) disliked black as adornment, because the Banu al-Abbas had adopted it as their garb and claimed to wear it in grief for al-Husayn ibn Ali. Had there been any merit in that claim, the duty to be first to it would have fallen on the Imams among his own descendants; and had they truly grieved for him as they claimed, they would not have treated his descendants as they did. The Imams therefore disliked adorning themselves in the garb of such people.

They saw no harm, however, in images or figures worked into garments. One of the companions of Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali narrated that he entered upon him while he was seated on a carpet bearing figures, and raised the matter with him. The Master said that the sunnah regarding such a carpet is that one tread upon it. When the dislike that some people hold for living figures was mentioned before him — on the grounds that Allah, mighty and exalted, created such things — he said: "Is it not He, mighty and exalted, who created everything: the trees and the inanimate, all that is seen? Yet they portray that and see no harm in portraying it. So what is the difference between the one and the other?"

---

**On Ornaments and What May Be Made of Them**

The Imams of the house of the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and his family — transmitted from him that he permitted women to adorn themselves with gold. When Jafar ibn Muhammad was asked about this, he said: "My father used to adorn his children and his women with gold and silver." He also said: "There is no harm in ornamenting swords and copies of the Quran with gold and silver."

It is narrated of Ali that he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, say: "A woman should not pray except with an earring upon her, or more" — meaning when she is able to obtain such a thing. He forbade women to leave themselves bare of ornament, and to imitate men, and he cursed those among them who did so.

Jafar ibn Muhammad said: "It is not fitting for a woman to leave herself unadorned, even if only by hanging a necklace about her neck."

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, also forbade women, when they go out, to wear ornaments that make an audible sound. This accords with the words of Allah, mighty and exalted:

﴿وَلَا يَضْرِبْنَ بِأَرْجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعْلَمَ مَا يُخْفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّ﴾

"And let them not strike their feet so as to make known what they conceal of their adornment." (Al-Nur: 31)

It is also narrated that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, forbade men from wearing a gold seal-ring. His own seal was of silver, its stone likewise silver, engraved with the words "Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah." He further forbade the wearing of iron rings and all adornment in iron, saying: "It is the ornament of the people of the Fire." It is narrated as well that he wore his ring on his right hand. The Imams followed the same practice, wearing their rings on the right hand and instructing their followers and companions to do likewise.

Ali narrated that he heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, say: "Whoever sets a ring with a stone of red carnelian, Allah seals his affair with what is good." The Prophet recommended it, and the ruby as well, and would say: "Each time a man looks into it, light increases upon his face, and the prayer wearing it is worth seventy prayers." He also said: "How excellent a stone is crystal." The engraving on Ali's seal read "Ali believes in Allah." Jafar ibn Muhammad forbade the setting of a ring whose stone bears an engraved figure, and the engraving on his own seal read "My Lord, You are my trust, so protect me from the evil of Your creation." It is further narrated that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, used to turn his ring so that the stone lay against the inside of his palm.

---

**On Fragrance, Its Excellence, and Its Recommendation**

From the Imams of the house of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, it is narrated through Ali that he said: "Three things were given to the prophets: fragrance, marriage, and the siwak." When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family, traveled, he carried certain things with him:

- the flask
- the shears
- the kohl-vessel
- the mirror
- the comb
- the siwak

He said, may Allah bless him and his family: "No servant's garment is cleansed but that his faults are lessened, and his scent is not made sweet but that his understanding is increased."

Jafar ibn Muhammad said: "A sweet fragrance strengthens the heart and increases vigor. The fragrance of men is that whose scent is apparent and whose color is hidden, and the fragrance of women is that whose color is apparent and whose scent is concealed — except when they go out, for then it is disliked that they perfume themselves so that it can be detected from them."

It is narrated of Ali that he said: the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, used to apply fragrance, and to apply it abundantly, until it would change the color of his hair. And he said, may Allah bless him and his family: "Whoever goes to the Friday prayer, let him apply perfume, even if only from his family's flask."

It is also narrated of Ali that he would sometimes perfume himself from the fragrance of his wives — by which is meant the kind of women's fragrance whose color does not show, only its scent. As for fragrance that shows its color, such as khaluq and the like, it is disliked for men except in the company of their wives.

The Imams disliked that one return a gift of fragrance to the one who offered it, and likewise that one refuse an offering of water.

Al-Muizz (ع) said: Al-Mansur, may Allah sanctify his soul, told him: One day, when he was a small boy, he was present at the table of al-Mahdi (ع). A company of al-Mahdi's sons and grandsons were eating before him, with a serving-girl standing by with water. She offered water to one of the boys, who refused it, and al-Mahdi rebuked her sharply and said: "Were it not for the sanctity of your sharing in this food, I would have disciplined you well. What moved you to offer him water when he had not asked for it?" Then he turned to the boy and said: "And you — when it was offered to you, why did you refuse it? Water is too noble a thing to be offered to one who did not ask, or to be refused by one to whom it is offered."

Al-Mansur (ع) said: "I did not understand at the time what manner of thing this was, but when I came to understand, I grasped his meaning. And so it is with fragrance as well."

From Ali it is narrated that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, used to anoint himself with musk, المسك. He held it in such regard that he directed it be placed in his embalming, his حنوط, so that its fragrance would remain with him — and something finer than it was also used over him in that embalming.

It is further narrated, on the authority of the Imams, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, forbade a woman to pray unless she has applied henna, الحناء, or has at least touched the place of the henna with something.

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali said that a woman should therefore not leave off the dye, الخضاب, even when she has grown old — even if she does no more than wipe her hand with henna as a light anointing. She should not make herself resemble men.

From Ali it is narrated that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: "It is not for a menstruating woman to tell a story or to engrave."

And from Ali: "The Children of Israel perished through stories, engravings, henna, and excessive ornamentation."

edits.body_md:
### What is lawful in hunting and what is forbidden

> أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ صَيْدُ ٱلْبَحْرِ وَطَعَامُهُۥ مَتَعًۭا لَّكُمْ وَلِلسَّيَّارَةِ ۖ وَحُرِّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ صَيْدُ ٱلْبَرِّ مَا دُمْتُمْ حُرُمًۭا

﴿أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ صَيْدُ الْبَحْرِ وَطَعَامُهُ مَتَاعًا لَكُمْ وَلِلسَّيَّارَةِ وَحُرِّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ صَيْدُ الْبَرِّ مَا دُمْتُمْ حُرُمًا﴾ "He has made permissible for you the hunting of the sea and its food, as a pleasure for you and for travelers, and forbidden for you is the hunting of land as long as you are in the sacred state" (al-Maidah: 96), and He said: ﴿وَإِذَا حَلَلْتُمْ فَاصْطَادُوا﴾ "But when you leave the sacred state, then hunt" (al-Maidah: 2). The Almighty thus permitted sea hunting even while one remains in the state of consecration, and forbade land hunting for the duration of it.

He addressed this to the generality of the believers, except for what was excluded from it on the tongue of His Messenger and the Imams of his household, who make plain what He intends, as He says: ﴿وَأَنزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ الذِّكْرَ لِتُبَيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ مَا نُزِّلَ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ "And We have sent down to you the Remembrance that you may make clear to the people what has been revealed to them" (al-Nahl: 44).

The Imams of the household of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, are reported to have forbidden the hunting of birds in their nests. He said: "The bird in its nest is under the protection of Allah; but if it takes to the air upon its wings, then hunt it if you wish. Set a trap for it and shoot at it." It is further narrated from him, and from Ali (ع), and from Jafar ibn Muhammad (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), that pigeons in towns should not be hunted, because they belong to their owners even when they fly free. What is lawful and what is forbidden among the beasts of land and sea has already been treated in the chapters on food. Whatever is caught of what is lawful to eat is eaten; whatever is caught of what is forbidden to eat is left and not eaten, except in a case of dire necessity for one who is compelled.

### What hunting animals seize and kill

> عَلَيْهِ ۖ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ

﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا أُحِلَّ لَهُمْ قُلْ أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ الطَّيِّبَاتُ وَمَا عَلَّمْتُم مِّنَ الْجَوَارِحِ مُكَلِّبِينَ تُعَلِّمُونَهُنَّ مِمَّا عَلَّمَكُمُ اللَّهُ فَكُلُوا مِمَّا أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَاذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ﴾ "They ask you what has been made lawful for them.

Say: Lawful for you are all good things, and what you have trained of hunting animals, training them as Allah has taught you, so eat of what they have caught for you, and mention the name of Allah over it, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning" (al-Maidah: 4).

The Imams of the household of the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace — transmitted from Ali, upon him be peace, that he said: if a hunting animal seizes prey and the prey dies before slaughter can be performed, then provided the animal is trained and a Muslim sent it forth and invoked the name of Allah at the moment of release, the prey may be eaten. If he forgot to invoke the name at the moment of release, he invokes it when he remembers. If he deliberately omitted it, however, the prey is not to be eaten.

The word الجوارح, in the Arabic tongue in which the Quran was revealed, means the earners. The Arabs say, "So-and-so is the جارحة of his household," meaning the one who earns for them. Dogs and their like, and the birds of prey used in hunting, are earners that earn the catch for those who have trained them. If such an animal is untrained yet seizes prey, and the prey is reached while still alive and then slaughtered, it may be eaten; but if slaughter cannot be reached in time, it may not be eaten.
