They — (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) — held that whatever trained hunting animals seize may be eaten, even if slaughter was not reached, and even if the animal has eaten from it. Every trained hunting creature, such as cheetahs and other land predators, as well as birds of prey, may have its catch eaten.

It is narrated from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, that concerning the hunting of the black dog, he disliked it for them and ordered that it be killed. They further held that all dogs are equal in their ruling, apart from this distinction, whether of the Kurdish kind or the greyhound kind: what they seize may be eaten when they are trained. They held as well that if the prey is reached while still alive and the hunting animal has wounded it, but the hunter does not then slaughter it and it dies in his hands from the wound the hunting animal inflicted, it may be eaten. If, however, the hunting animal did not wound it, and it was carried off and died afterward, it may not be eaten.

From Ali comes a prohibition on eating any game that dies before slaughter can be reached — whether taken by the dogs of the Magians, by the Arabs who are Christians, or by any hunting animal they have trained — unless Muslims afterward retrain those animals.

### What hunters bring down with a throw

> ٱعْتَدَىٰ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَلَهُۥ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌۭ

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَيَبْلُوَنَّكُمُ اللَّهُ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنَ الصَّيْدِ تَنَالُهُ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَرِمَاحُكُمْ لِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ مَن يَخَافُهُ بِالْغَيْبِ فَمَنِ اعْتَدَى بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَلَهُ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ "O you who believe, Allah will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and your spears can reach, that Allah may know who fears Him in the unseen. So whoever transgresses after that, for him is a painful punishment" (al-Maidah: 94).

One of the Imams of the household of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked by a man about hunting — specifically, about throwing at prey, striking it, and having it die. The Imam said: "Eat what you have killed outright (al-isma), and do not eat what you have driven off (al-inma)."

Al-isma is when a man throws at quarry, strikes it, and it dies on the spot. Al-inma is when he strikes it and it moves off, passing out of his sight until it is hidden from him and disappears, and then it dies and he finds it dead — with no way of knowing whether it died from his blow or from something else.

It has been narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad that he said: if a hunter shoots game with an arrow, strikes it in a fatal spot, and it then disappears from him, yet he later finds his arrow in it and knows from that it died from his shot, he may eat it. If he does not know that, he may not eat it.

From Ali it has been narrated that he said: if a hunter shoots game, strikes it, and it then falls from a height or falls into water and dies, he may not eat it — unless he knows with certainty that it died from the blow that struck it.

Whatever has been mentioned of game struck or killed by a projectile is lawful to eat only when it has been struck with a sword, a spear, an arrow, or an iron implement. Anything struck with a stick, a stone, or a pellet may not be eaten — according to the position of the people of the household — unless it is reached while still alive and properly slaughtered. They permitted the مِعْراض when a hunter has no other arrow: the مِعْراض is a featherless arrow thrown so that it strikes game with its body. From Ali it has been narrated that he said: whatever a snare takes of game, if it dies in the snare before being slaughtered, may not be eaten. But if the snare severs a hand, a leg, or a limb, and the animal is then reached and slaughtered while still alive, it may be eaten — except for the severed limb itself. The الحبالة is any device set up to take game, such as nets, traps, and the like.

### The Comprehensive Doors of Slaughter

### The acts of those who slaughter

It has been narrated from the Imams of the household of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, that they transmitted from him that he said: "Whoever slaughters an animal, let him sharpen his blade and let him give his animal ease."

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, (ع), said: "When you intend to slaughter an animal, do not torment the beast. Sharpen the blade, face the qiblah, and invoke the name of Allah, and do not sever it through until it dies — meaning do not cut off its head." He likewise forbade that an animal be skinned until it has died and grown still.

On the matter of the invocation, the teaching is as follows: whoever slaughters and forgets to invoke the name of Allah, or forgets to face the animal toward the qiblah, or is simply unaware of the requirement, should invoke the name of Allah the Almighty when he remembers, and the slaughtered animal may be eaten. But if he deliberately omits it, the slaughter is not permissible to eat. If he says "There is no god but Allah," or "Allah is the Greatest," or remembers Allah the Almighty by whatever words he uses, that suffices in place of the full invocation. What the Imams recommended to say at the moment of slaughter is: "In the name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest."

It is also narrated from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, that he forbade mutilating beasts and commanded that they be slaughtered as is their due. He further forbade المجثمة and الْمَصْبُورَةُ — that is, an animal that is held captive, or buried, or tied in place and then shot at until it dies.

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali said: "Whoever kills a sparrow without cause, Allah the Almighty will bring it before him on the Day of Resurrection, and it will cry out: 'My Lord, ask this one why he killed me without slaughter.'"

Mutilation, then, is a grave matter.

The Master said: Slaughter belongs at the place of slaughter — that is, below the غلصمة. The غلصمة is the knot in the windpipe, and it is to be left in the head. The slaughterer cuts the windpipe, the gullet, and the two jugular veins, falling short of none of these, and without cutting into the bone. That is the Sunnah of slaughter. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali — and upon his family — was asked about breaking an animal's neck before it dies, and he disapproved of it. It was said: if the knife outruns the slaughterer, or if out of ignorance he cuts off the animal's head without intending it and without knowing that this is not permitted, there is nothing against him and the animal may be eaten. But if he does so deliberately, he has done wrong, and the animal is not to be eaten.

It was further said: if the beast bolts — that is, flees or refuses — so that it cannot be slaughtered, or if it falls into a well and cannot be lifted out, nor can one reach the place of slaughter, then let it be stabbed with a spear, struck with a sword, or struck with an iron implement until it dies, and it may be eaten. It was said: there is no valid slaughter except with iron. One may not slaughter with a stone, nor a tooth, nor a nail, nor a bone, nor anything else — only with iron.

### What may be eaten of slaughtered animals and what may not

The Imams of the household of the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace — are reported to have disliked the slaughter of a milk-giving animal or a pregnant one, though they did not forbid it outright. The dislike arose from the benefit such animals hold for one who has nothing else.

> فَكُلُوا۟ مِمَّا ذُكِرَ ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ إِن

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali was asked about the slaughtered animals of the Jews, the Christians, the Magians, and those of divergent belief. In reply, he recited the word of Allah the Almighty: ﴿فَكُلُوا مِمَّا ذُكِرَ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ إِن كُنتُم بِآيَاتِهِ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — "So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs" (al-Anam: 118). He then said: "When you hear them invoking the name of Allah, then eat; and what they do not invoke the name of Allah over, do not eat. And if any among them is suspected of omitting the invocation, believing it permissible to do so, his slaughtered animal need not be eaten — unless one is present at the moment of slaughter and hears him invoke the name of Allah the Almighty over it."

Jafar ibn Muhammad said: "There is no harm in meat sold in the markets of the Muslims, so long as it is not known of the slaughterers that they depart from the Sunnah in their slaughter, and so long as no such departure has been witnessed in their practice."

The scholars of this tradition held a dislike for slaughtered animals offered by Magians and by Arab Christians. They permitted slaughter performed by a blind man, provided he is directed toward the qiblah and slaughters correctly; likewise by a woman, when she does so correctly; and by a boy who has not yet reached maturity, when he does so correctly and there is genuine need of him. They saw no harm in slaughter performed without ritual purity. They also permitted slaughter by a mute person, provided he understands the invocation and signals it by gesture.

### Valid and invalid slaughter

From the Imams of the household of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, it is transmitted that Ali was asked about the fetuses of livestock whose mothers are slaughtered while the fetuses remain in the womb — whether they become lawful when brought out. He said: "Their slaughter is the slaughter of their mothers, for the fetus is one of her limbs. But if it comes out alive, it is left until it dies, and then it may be eaten, provided it has grown hair or fur — or has something of that upon it, even on its tail, for the tail is the first place where hair appears." He disliked any fetus that had not yet grown hair or fur.

He was then asked about limbs cut from a living animal — the fatty tails of sheep, the humps of camels, and the like. He said: "Whatever is cut from them and separated while they are still alive, before slaughter, is carrion and may not be eaten — and the rest of the animal may not be eaten when it is slaughtered."

He also said that valid slaughter is recognized by four signs:

- the eye flickering
- the leg kicking
- the tail moving
- the ear stirring

Any animal that moves, thrashes, flickers its eye, or shows any motion after the knife has been drawn across it has been validly slaughtered. An animal that falls and is slaughtered without any movement at all may not be eaten, even if blood flows from it.

The Master was asked about an animal that is properly slaughtered and then falls from a height or into water and dies. He said: "If you have done the slaughter well and fulfilled what is required of it, then eat."

From Jafar ibn Muhammad: the Sunnah for large animals is that they be sacrificed standing, with one leg bound. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, sacrificed his gift-offering in that manner. If that is not possible, there is no harm in the animal kneeling and being hobbled. He disliked that the sheep be slaughtered standing, except when there is a reason, and held the Sunnah to be that it is laid on its side. If a sheep is sacrificed in the manner of large animals, however, there is no harm in that either.

He was asked about an animal slaughtered from behind the nape of the neck. He said that if the slaughterer was unaware, there is no harm; but if he did so intentionally, knowing the Sunnah, the animal may not be eaten and he is to be corrected.

He was asked about two sheep — one validly slaughtered and the other not — when it is unknown which of the two was valid. He said that neither is to be eaten until the valid one is identified.

### The sacrificial offerings

The Imams of the household of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, transmitted — and the Messenger himself transmitted — that he addressed the people before the Day of Sacrifice and said: "O people, whoever has the means, let him sacrifice and let him magnify the rites of Allah. And whoever does not have the means, then Allah the Almighty does not burden a soul beyond its capacity."

A man of the Ansar met the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, on the Day of Sacrifice, after the prayer had concluded, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you would honor me with your presence today — I have prepared food for you." The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, went with him. The man brought out the food and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I slaughtered my sacrifice before going out to the place of prayer, and I instructed my family to prepare this meal, so that I might be the first to bring it to you." The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said to him: "Your sheep is a sheep of meat. If you have another, sacrifice that one in its place." The man said: "I have nothing but a young goat of mine." He said: "Then sacrifice it — though this will not be lawful for anyone who comes after you."

The Sunnah holds that the sacrifice is not slaughtered until after the Eid prayer on the Day of Sacrifice. Whoever slaughters before the prayer, that act does not count as a valid sacrifice, and he must repeat it when he is able. The best time to slaughter is the Day of Sacrifice itself, though the sacrifice remains valid throughout the days of Mina — the Day of Sacrifice and the three days that follow it. Jafar ibn Muhammad said that among camels and cattle, nothing suffices as a sacrifice except the mature animal, and the same applies to goats; the yearling of sheep, however, suffices. He also said that the sacrifice is an obligation upon every Muslim who has the means, and that a single sacrifice on a man's part suffices for his entire household.

It is narrated from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, that he addressed the people on the Day of Sacrifice and said: "This is the day of العَجّ and الثَّجّ. الثَّجّ is the blood you pour out, and whoever's intention is sincere, its first drop is an expiation for every sin. And العَجّ is supplication, so cry out to Allah the Almighty. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, no one will leave this standing-place except that he is forgiven — save the one persisting in a great sin among the great sins, who does not bring himself to forsake it."

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family, entered upon Fatimah, (ع), on the Day of Sacrifice and said: "O Fatimah, arise and witness your sacrifice, for its very first drop of blood is an expiation for every sin that is yours. Its flesh, its dung, its bones, its wool — everything of it — will be placed in your balance and multiplied for you seventy times over." Al-Miqdad heard this and said: "May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah — is this something singled out for the family of Muhammad, or is it general?" He said: "Rather, it is for the Muslims in general."

Jafar ibn Muhammad said that what is recommended for a man is that he undertake the slaughter of his sacrifice with his own hand. If he is unable to do so, he should place his hand alongside the hand of the slaughterer. If he is unable to do even that, he should stand over it, invoking the name of Allah upon it until it is slaughtered. From Ali it is reported that he said: a Muslim's sacrifice should not be slaughtered except by a Muslim, who says at the moment of slaughter: "In the name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. I have turned my face toward the One who created the heavens and the earth, upright and submitting, and I am not among the polytheists. Truly my prayer, my sacrifice, my living, and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds, who has no partner. By this I have been commanded, and I am the first of those who submit."

From Ja'far ibn Muhammad it is reported that he was asked about the best sacrificial animals. He replied: "The females of camels, then their males, then the females of cattle, then their males, then the rams of sheep, then the wethers" — meaning those whose testicles have been crushed or bound until they spoil — "then the ewes, then the male of the goats, then the females of them." He held in low regard any animal whose ears had been cut off. Among all these, the best is the fattest and the largest. The finest of rams is the horned ram that eats amid blackness, drinks amid blackness, walks amid blackness, looks amid blackness, urinates amid blackness, and drops dung amid blackness. It was with such an animal that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, used to sacrifice. That ram is the الأملح — the black-and-white. It is transmitted that he sacrificed with two such black-and-white rams, and it is said that this is the very description of the ram sent down to Ibrahim, (ع) and upon his family.

It is transmitted from Jafar ibn Muhammad that he permitted sharing in a sacrifice for one who cannot find an animal to offer alone but is able to contribute to a shared offering. From Ali, it is transmitted that he disliked sacrificing an animal with a broken horn, one that is clearly lame, one that is clearly emaciated, or one whose ear has been wholly cut away. He permitted a slit ear when it is a distinguishing mark, and an aged animal when it carries no defect or leanness. He said: "Whoever buys a sacrifice and it falls ill or dies before the Day of Sacrifice, it has sufficed for him; but if he obtains another to sacrifice in its place and does so, that is better."

> فَكُلُوا۟ مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا۟ ٱلْقَانِعَ وَٱلْمُعْتَرَّ

It is transmitted from Jafar ibn Muhammad that he was asked about the word of Allah the Almighty, ﴿فَكُلُوا مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا الْقَانِعَ وَالْمُعْتَرَّ﴾ — "So eat of it and feed the contented and the petitioner" (al-Hajj: 36) — and about His word, ﴿فَكُلُوا مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا الْبَائِسَ الْفَقِيرَ﴾ — "So eat of it and feed the wretched poor" (al-Hajj: 28). He said: "The قانع is the beggar who is content with what he is given and does not deem it too little; the مُعْتَرّ is the one who presents himself for charity but does not ask; the poor man is the one who finds nothing; and the مسكين is harder pressed than he in his condition — and the wretched poor man is the worst of them all in condition and the most hard pressed."

The speaker recounted that his father — رض — when slaughtering his sacrifice at Mina or offering a gift-offering, would set the head of the animal before him. Whenever a beggar passed, he would stop the man and say, "Take the head." If the beggar took it gladly and went on his way, he gave it to him. If the beggar took it but showed reluctance, he would say, "Leave it," and give him meat instead. And if the beggar turned away from it and refused it altogether, he left him with nothing — testing by this the true condition of each poor man who came before him.

> فَكُلُوا۟ مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا۟ ٱلْقَانِعَ وَٱلْمُعْتَرَّ

It is related from Ali that he said, concerning the word of God Almighty — ﴿فَكُلُوا مِنْهَا﴾ "So eat of it" (al-Hajj: 36) — "This is a command of recommendation, not of obligation. Whoever wishes may eat of his sacrifice, and whoever wishes need not eat of it; and to eat of it is better."

It has also come down from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, that he made Ali a partner in a gift-offering consisting of one hundred sacrificial camels. He gave the order that a piece be taken from each camel, placed in a pot, and cooked. He then called Ali, and the two of them ate of the meat as much as they could manage and drank of the broth, so that they might partake of every one of the animals. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "The broth is one of the two meats, for the strength of the meat passes out into it."

Jafar ibn Muhammad was then asked...

Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) was asked about a man whom the fear of Allah Almighty had so overwhelmed that he abandoned women, abandoned wholesome food, and could no longer lift his head toward heaven out of reverence for Allah Almighty. The one who posed the question said, "As for his turning away from women, I know what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had of them. As for his turning away from wholesome food, the Messenger of Allah used to eat meat and honey. And as for the fear of Allah Almighty overtaking him until he could no longer raise his head toward the sky out of reverence — who was ever more fearful of Allah, or more humbled before Him, than the Messenger of Allah? Yet he did not do this." For Allah Almighty has said, *"Indeed in the Messenger of Allah you have a good example,"* and true humility resides in the heart.

> إِن يَكُونُوا۟ فُقَرَآءَ يُغْنِهِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِۦ

The merits of marriage are to be understood in this spirit, for there is no monasticism in Islam. Allah Almighty said: *"And marry the unmarried among you and the righteous among your male and female slaves. If they should be poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing."*

The Imams of the House of the Messenger of Allah transmitted that he said: "Whoever loves to follow my way among my nation, let him know that marriage is one of my Sunnahs." And he said: "Whoever loves to meet Allah pure and purified, let him meet Him with a wife." And he said: "There is no young man who marries in his youth except that his devil cries out, Woe to him, he has protected two-thirds of his religion! So let the servant then fear Allah Almighty in the remaining third." Whenever he learned that one of his companions had married, he would say, "He has completed his religion." And he said, (ع), "The more a believer increases in faith, the more he loves women." And he said, "There is no monasticism in Islam. Marry, for I shall boast of your numbers before the nations." He forbade celibacy and the forsaking of marriage.

He said: "When a believing man comes to his believing wife, two angels enfold him, and he is like one who has drawn his sword in the path of Allah. When he is done, his sins fall from him as the leaves fall from the tree, as though he had washed himself clean of sin. If she conceives by him, he has the reward of one who fasts and stands in prayer. When the pangs of labor seize her, no one knows her reward but Allah Almighty. When she delivers, with every draft of milk she suckles the child, Allah Almighty writes for her a good deed and erases from her an evil one. And if she should die of her travail, she will rise on the Day of Resurrection without reckoning, for she died of her affliction."

The Master said: "Whoever abandons marriage out of fear of household expense has thought ill of his Lord the Almighty, who says, *If they should be poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty.*" He also said: "Whoever amasses wealth and does not marry, so that the women left unwed because of him fall into sin, their sin rests upon him." From Jafar ibn Muhammad comes this: "No two believers are joined in a lawful marriage but that a caller from heaven cries out, Allah Almighty has wedded such a one to such a one; and no two believing spouses are parted from a marriage but that a caller from heaven cries out, Allah Almighty has permitted the separation of such a one from such a one."

On what is recommended in a spouse, and from whose marriage one should turn away, it is narrated from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah that he said: "Choose well for your seed, for the maternal uncle is one of the two who share the bed." His meaning was that seed should be placed nowhere but in purity — that the child's mother be neither of corrupt origin nor corrupt in herself. From this same principle he forbade that a child be suckled by the milk of a wicked woman. If such a thing is disliked in nursing and forbidden there, then in lineage it is graver still, and the prohibition more emphatic. He said: "Marry those who are your equals, and give your daughters in marriage to them, and choose well for your seed."

He related that Allah Almighty says: "When I wish to grant My servant the good of this world and the Hereafter, I give him a tongue that remembers Me, a humble heart, a body patient in affliction, and a believing wife who gladdens him when he looks upon her and guards herself and his wealth in his absence." And he said: "Five things are of happiness: a righteous wife, upright children, righteous companions, a man's provision in his own land, and love for the family of Muhammad, (ع) and his family."

He said: "A good woman among women is like the albino crow, and the albino crow is seldom found." By "good" he meant the believing, chaste, and beautiful woman — fitting in every one of her states. Such a woman is rare, and so he likened her to the albino crow, the rarest of birds. He said: "A woman of standing has no price, neither the good among them nor the bad. As for the good, she has no price in gold or silver or all the possessions of this world; and as for the bad, she has no price, not even of dust, for dust is better than she." And he said: "The world is but enjoyment, and the best enjoyment of the world is a righteous wife." And he said: "Of the believing man's happiness is a righteous wife, a spacious dwelling, an easy mount, and a righteous child."

He forbade marrying a woman for her wealth or her beauty alone, saying, "Her wealth makes her overbearing, and her beauty destroys her." And he said: "Take the one of religion." And he said, comparing what is most prized: "There is no horse finer than the deep black, and no woman like the daughter of one's age." And he said: "The best of your women are the women of Quraysh, the most tender toward a husband and the most devoted to a child."

He said: "Marry the one of clear, healthy complexion, for there is blessing in that. And when one of you would marry a woman, let him ask about her hair as he asks about her face, for the hair is one of the two beauties. And keep to those of shorter stature, for that is better suited to what you seek." He said: "A woman is but a necklace, so let each of you consider well with what he adorns himself." And he said: "If there is ill fortune in anything, it is in a woman, a dwelling, and a mount."

He said: "Women are four: a gathering that gathers, a spring that gives water, a war that subdues, and a galling fetter."

The galling fetter requires explanation. In the Age of Ignorance, captors would bind those they wished to torment with a thong of fresh hide stripped from a camel, turned hair-inward against the skin and bound fast. As the hide dried it contracted, pulling tighter and tighter; lice would breed within it and could not be reached because of the tightness, and so the captive suffered enormously — a torment that struck without a single blow. This is the image the Prophet ﷺ applied to the bad wife and to what her husband endures at her hands.

The remaining three are:

- **A gathering that gathers:** a woman in whom goodness and purity are gathered together.
- **A spring that gives water:** a woman who holds one child in her arms and carries another in her womb.
- **A war that subdues:** a woman of ill manners toward her husband.

> وَلَدٌۭ ۚ فَإِن كَانَ لَكُمْ وَلَدٌۭ فَلَهُنَّ ٱلثُّمُنُ مِمَّا تَرَكْتُم ۚ مِّنۢ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍۢ تُوصُونَ بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍۢ ۗ وَإِن كَانَ رَجُلٌۭ يُورَثُ كَلَلَةً أَوِ ٱمْرَأَةٌۭ وَلَهُۥٓ أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌۭ فَلِكُلِّ وَحِدٍۢ مِّنْهُمَا ٱلسُّدُسُ ۚ فَإِن كَانُوٓا۟ أَكْثَرَ مِن ذَلِكَ فَهُمْ شُرَكَآءُ فِى ٱلثُّلُثِ ۚ مِنۢ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍۢ يُوصَىٰ بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍ غَيْرَ مُضَآرٍّۢ ۚ وَصِيَّةًۭ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَلِيمٌۭ

He said: "Beware of marrying the foolish woman, for her companionship is an affliction and her child is a loss." And he said: "The best women of my nation are those fairest of face and lightest in dowry." And he said: "Among the blessings of a woman is that her firstborn be a girl." He said again: "Women are four: a spring that gives water, a gathering that gathers, a war that subdues, and a barren woman." And he said: "Marry the dark-complexioned woman who is fertile, and do not marry the beautiful barren woman, for I will boast of your numbers before the nations on the Day of Resurrection. The children who die young are beneath the Throne of the Most Merciful, seeking forgiveness for their parents; Ibrahim, (ع), takes them into his care, and Sarah raises them upon a mountain of musk and amber and saffron."

He said: "The best of your women is the ardent yet chaste one, ardent toward her husband and chaste from all besides him." And he said: "Marry the virgins, for they are sweetest of mouth, purest of womb, quickest of the women to learn, and most steadfast in affection." And he said: "Marry the *ayyami*" — meaning Allah Almighty will better their character, broaden their provision, and increase their blessing. His command here is to marry the *ayyami*, those women who once had husbands who died or who divorced them, and it is a command of encouragement, not of obligation that may not be left, just as Allah's word, *"And marry the unmarried among you,"* is of this kind. Whoever marries one of the *ayyami*, desiring what Allah Almighty and His Messenger have urged, has done what he was called to; and whoever marries a virgin, there is no fault in that, for the virtue of marrying virgins has already been mentioned from the Messenger of Allah. Yet the *ayyami* should not be passed over out of mere preference or disdain on account of a prior marriage, for most of the wives of the Messenger of Allah had been married before, and Allah Almighty says: *"Indeed in the Messenger of Allah you have a good example for those who hope for Allah and the Last Day."*

> إِن يَكُونُوا۟ فُقَرَآءَ يُغْنِهِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِۦ

A Muslim must respond to his Muslim brother who comes forward as a suitor, provided he is satisfied with that man's religion. He warned that to refuse such a proposal invites strife and grave corruption across the land. He forbade marriage sought for any purpose other than the face of Allah Almighty and the preservation of chastity, and he forbade marriage undertaken for show or reputation. He said: "Whoever marries a woman for her standing or her wealth, Allah leaves him to that; but whoever marries her for her religion and her excellence, Allah Almighty grants him beauty and wealth besides." He then recited the words of Allah Almighty: *"If they should be poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty, and Allah is all-Encompassing, Knowing."* And he said: "There is no calamity heavier upon a servant in his religion than that his Muslim kinsman should come to him and say, Marry me your daughter, and he answer, I will not, because he is wealthier than the suitor."

It is told of Ali ibn al-Husayn (ع) that he passed a woman in one of the districts of Makkah and was struck by her beauty and character. He inquired about her, learned she had no husband, proposed, married her, and consummated the marriage. Afterward, a kinsman came to him and said, "O son of the Messenger of Allah, something concerning your marriage to this woman has weighed upon me, for you married her without asking after her lineage. I could not rest until I looked into the matter myself. I found her to be of the Banu Shayban, among the noblest of her people, and so I was gladdened and set at ease."

Ali ibn al-Husayn asked, "And what was it you had feared?"

The man replied, "I feared she might not be your equal, and that people would speak of it."

Ali ibn al-Husayn said to him, "I had thought you of sounder judgment than this. Do you not know that Allah Almighty brought Islam, and by it raised the lowly, completed what was deficient, and ennobled what was base? There is no reproach upon the affair of a Muslim; reproach belongs only to the Age of Ignorance."

He also married a freedwoman who had borne a son to a man now dead. When Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan heard of it, he wrote to reproach him, believing he had found grounds for fault, saying, "Was there not enough for you among the women of Quraysh and the noble Arabs to keep you from the mother of another man's son?"

Ali ibn al-Husayn wrote back to him: "To proceed: Allah Almighty has by Islam raised the lowly and completed the deficient, so there is no reproach upon the affair of a Muslim; reproach belongs only to the Age of Ignorance. And the Messenger of Allah married such a one" — meaning Safiyyah bint Hayy ibn Akhtab — "and in him is a good example."

Were it permissible to disdain the mothers of children, the marriage bed would be abandoned and corruption would appear in the land. The Imams — عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ — are the most fit to make this plain, so that the people might follow their example.

Allah Almighty said: *"O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most honored of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Aware."*

On the day of the conquest of Makkah, he addressed the people, praised and glorified Allah, then said: "O people, Allah Almighty has taken from you the arrogance of the Age of Ignorance and its boasting in forefathers. You are all from Adam, and Adam was from clay. The best of Allah's servants before Allah are those most fearful of Him. Arabness is not a thing born of a father; it is a tongue that speaks. Whoever is held back by his deeds, his lineage will not advance him." Every claim of blood or rancor from the Age of Ignorance lay beneath his feet until the Day of Resurrection.

It is told that he gave Dubaa bint al-Zubayr ibn Abd al-Muttalib in marriage to al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, and said that he had done so only to make marriage humble — so that the people might follow the example of the Messenger of Allah and know that the most honored among them before Allah is the most God-fearing. Al-Zubayr was the brother of Abd Allah, the father of the Prophet — — by both father and mother. Jafar ibn Muhammad said: "The Messenger of Allah married Qurayshi women to freedmen: he gave Dubaa bint al-Zubayr ibn Abd al-Muttalib to al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, and he married Tamim al-Dari to a woman of the Banu Hashim ibn Abd Manaf."

The Messenger of Allah said: "When one whose religion and trustworthiness are pleasing to you comes seeking marriage, then marry him; for if you do not, there will be strife in the earth and great corruption."

It is narrated from Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad that he was in Makkah when word reached him that Dawud ibn Ali had ordered the killing of al-Maali ibn Hunaish — one of his own companions — and that the killing had been carried out. Al-Sadiq (ع) rose in anger, dragging his garment behind him. His son Ismail (ع) came to meet him and said: "O my father, where are you going? The people are defiant, and their insolence against Allah Almighty is such as you well know. Leave them be." Al-Sadiq struck him upon the chest and said: "Step aside from me. Were it a blazing fire, I would plunge into it." He went on until he came in upon Dawud and said: "O Dawud, you have committed a sin that Allah will never forgive you." Dawud said: "And what is that?" He said: "You have killed a believing man from among the people of Paradise."

Dawud grew angry and fell silent for a time, then said: "And you too have committed a sin that Allah Almighty will not forgive you." He said: "And what is that?" He said: "Your daughter has been given in marriage to a man from Banu Umayyah." Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad answered that in this his example was the Messenger of Allah himself: the Messenger had given his daughter Zaynab in marriage to Abu al-As ibn Rabiah, and he had given Umm Kulthum in marriage to Uthman ibn Affan, and when she died he married Uthman to Ruqayyah — both being his daughters and his family.

Then he said: "You are the one who forbade the killing of believers unjustly." Dawud said: "I did not command that he be killed." Al-Sadiq said that al-Sarraqi had reported, "We have lost him," and that the killer himself had said, "I have taken responsibility for him." Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad then had his companions seize the man and bring him forward to be put to death. The man cried out: "O servants of Allah, do you command me to kill men for them, and then exact retribution from me?" Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad said: "As for you, O enemy of Allah, you confess to the killing, and your companion has denied that he commanded you to it. Have you any proof of that?" The man said: "And who will bear witness for me against Dawud?" He said: "Then retribution from you is obligatory and must be exacted." And he delivered him over to the kinsmen of al-Maali, and they put him to death.

Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad was asked whether it was permissible to give daughters in marriage to men of opposing views. He answered that the Messenger of Allah had given his own daughters in marriage to certain men who were known to them, and that Umar had sought the hand of Ali's daughter Umm Kulthum (ع), only for Ali to refuse him. Umar then went to al-Abbas and laid his grievance before him, pressing the Banu Abd al-Muttalib hard on the matter. Al-Abbas came to Ali (ع) and said: "O son of my brother, you see the position we are in. Umar has sought her hand and has pressed us hard over your refusal." He continued in this way until Ali finally committed her affair to him, whereupon al-Abbas gave her in marriage to Umar on his behalf.

It is therefore preferable to give daughters in marriage to people of sound faith, or at least to those who do not stir up enmity against the family of the Messenger of Allah. The marriage of a believer is better than any other, yet where necessity exists there is no harm in contracting marriage with Muslims of differing views. Marrying among them is likewise not forbidden in the way that marriage to polytheists is forbidden. The meritorious and preferred course, however, is marriage among people of sound faith; after them come the weak ones who are neither loyal nor hostile.

> فَإِن طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَن شَىْءٍۢ مِّنْهُ

A man asked Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali about his wife's sister — a believing woman of knowledge living in Basra with no male guardian among her kin to oversee her affairs. Abu Jafar said to him: "Do not give her in marriage to them. As for yourselves, there is no harm in giving the weak women in marriage to them; but a Nasibiyyah, the daughter of a Nasib — no."

Zurara ibn Ayan asked Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad about the same matter, and he likewise permitted giving the weak women in marriage to them, but not a Nasibiyyah, the daughter of a Nasib.

Abu Jafar also said to Zurara ibn Ayan concerning the weak women: "Keep to the simple and weak among women."

And Abu Jafar said: "Marry into the people of doubt, but do not give your women to them in marriage, for a woman takes on her husband's manners, and he prevails over her in the matter of his religion."

The Master said: "Marriage among the people of knowledge, and to them, is foremost, best, and nearest to Allah Almighty. If that is not to be had, then the weak ones — those who are neither loyal nor hostile — are better than the people of enmity."

After them come the Muslims of the people of truce, whom the Shariah binds together: they marry one another, inherit from one another, and the testimony of one of them concerning another is admissible, provided they are upright and free from suspicion. As for the people of disbelief — Jews, Christians, and polytheists — it is not lawful for any of them to marry a Muslim woman, though marriage among themselves is permissible. Muslim men may marry their women when necessity requires it and Muslim women are not to be found. Muslim women, however, are not lawful to them.

Abu Abd Allah, (ع), was asked about the saying of Allah Almighty: ﴿الزَّانِي لَا يَنْكِحُ إِلَّا زَانِيَةً أَوْ مُشْرِكَةً وَالزَّانِيَةُ لَا يَنْكِحُهَا إِلَّا زَانٍ أَوْ مُشْرِكٌ وَحُرِّمَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — "The adulterer shall not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress shall not marry except an adulterer or a polytheist, and that is forbidden to the believers."

He said: "This was revealed concerning women known for licentiousness in the time of ignorance, who were openly hired out for adultery and had set up houses marked for that purpose. The truce came with the provision that whoever wished might return to them. Among them were Habibah, al-Rabab, and Sarah — the last of whom the Messenger of Allah and his family declared lawful to be killed on the day of the conquest of Makkah, because she had been inciting the polytheists to fight the Messenger of Allah and his family. As for a slave girl who has fallen into fornication, there is no harm in purchasing her and having relations with her, and there is likewise no harm in marrying such a woman when necessity requires it, provided one is fortified and guarded against her. Yet chaste women are better and more fitting."

A man came to the Messenger of Allah and his family and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have a woman who does not turn away the hand of one who touches her, and I love her." The Master said: "Then keep her."

It was narrated of a man who saw his wife committing adultery yet was loath to part from her: he may keep her if he wishes.

He was asked about a man marrying an immoral woman, and he said: "What prevents him? But if he does so, let him fortify the door of his house."

He was asked about a man who marries a slave girl born of adultery, and he said: "There is no harm in it, though to keep clear of that is dearer to me."

Concerning a man who has a slave girl who has fallen into fornication, asking whether he may have relations with her, he said: "Yes, if he wishes."

Concerning a man who marries a woman without full discernment, he said: "It is permissible, so long as no fault remains attached to his child."

Concerning a child of adultery — whether one may have relations with her, sell her if she is a slave girl, and buy her — he said: "Yes; the forbidden does not render the lawful forbidden, nor corrupt it. Were people to turn away from the like of these and forbid their marriage, corruption in the land would multiply, and Allah may yet set right the corrupters and accept the repentance of the sinners."

One of the Ahl al-Bayt (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) was asked about the saying of Allah Almighty, "The adulterer shall not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist." He said: "The word *marry* here may mean the act of union and intercourse, or it may mean the contract and marriage. If it means union and intercourse, then it may indeed signify adultery, not lawful marriage." He said: "As for His words, *except an adulterer or a polytheist* — a man does not bring upon himself the wrath of Allah Almighty in this except while he is a polytheist." And the Messenger of Allah said: "The adulterer does not commit adultery at the moment of his adultery while he is a believer."

**Mentioning the Seeking of Women's Hands in Marriage**

The Imams of the household of the Messenger of Allah are reported to have forbidden a man to propose marriage over his brother's proposal, and to bid over his brother's bid. Some of the Ahl al-Bayt explained this teaching: the prohibition on proposing over a brother's proposal applies only after mutual approach, contentment, inclination, attentiveness, and agreement have all been established — so that nothing remains but the contract itself. Where matters have not yet reached that point, there is no harm in two men, or a group, proposing to a woman until she inclines toward one of them and answers him; only at that moment does it become disliked for another to press a rival proposal. The same principle governs commerce: it is permissible for a man to bid on a commodity and for another to bid above him, so long as the two parties to the sale have not yet reached agreement.

The Messenger of Allah commanded selling by open auction, and people have continued ever since to outbid one another, each raising upon the other until the commodity is settled and the seller accepts a buyer. After that, no further bid should be made, nor any raising upon what has already been agreed. This is a matter of recommendation, on account of the benefit it carries. Should a suitor propose, or a bidder raise his bid on a commodity, after agreement has been reached but before the contract of marriage or sale is concluded, the same ruling applies: if one surpasses another in merit before the contract is concluded, it does not invalidate the marriage or the sale, since nothing has yet become binding on another party by contract. The Messenger of Allah said: "When one of you wishes to marry a woman, let him cast his gaze upon her, for he is but a buyer." And he said: "When one of you wishes to marry a woman, there is no harm in his looking at what draws him to her."

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali said that he mentioned this hadith to Jabir ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari, and Jabir said: "I heard it from the Messenger of Allah. I sought the hand of a young woman from among the women of the Ansar, and I concealed myself for her behind a wall of her father's garden, and I looked at her and saw what I wished to see and what I had not meant to see, and she pleased me, so I married her, and she was the best of women."

> قُل لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّوا۟ مِنْ أَبْصَرِهِمْ

Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad said: There is no harm in a man who wishes to marry a woman looking at her. He should not, however, look at a slave girl without her master's permission, since the master may have no wish to sell her or to present her.

The permission granted by the Messenger of Allah — allowing a man to look at the woman he intends to marry — extends that gaze to the point where he has learned that her family will give her to him and will not refuse him: where agreement has been reached and only the marriage contract remains. Even then, he should look only to acquaint himself with her condition, not out of any desire to look at her or to take pleasure in doing so. He must not deliberately direct his gaze toward her private parts or toward anything it is not fitting to see.

It is not lawful for a man to look with the eye of contemplation at women who are not his — meaning women other than his wives, those forbidden to him by blood relation, and those his right hand possesses — whether they appear bareheaded or unveiled. Allah, exalted be He, says: ﴿قُل لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّوا مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِمْ﴾ — "Say to the believing men that they lower their gaze."

Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad was asked about a man past whom a woman walks, and who looks at her from behind. He said: "Would it please any of you that men should look upon his womenfolk and his kinswomen? Be content for others with what you are content with for yourselves."

He also spoke about the words of Allah Almighty in the story of Moses — quoting what the woman said: ﴿قَالَتْ إِحْدَاهُمَا يَا أَبَتِ اسْتَأْجِرْهُ إِنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ اسْتَأْجَرْتَ الْقَوِيُّ الْأَمِينُ﴾ — "One of the two women said: O my father, hire him; indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy." He explained that she was speaking of Moses (ع) and his character. Her father said to her: "As for your saying that he is strong, that is evident from what you saw of his lifting the rock from the well. But how did you come to know his trustworthiness?" She said: "When he set out with me to come to you, I wished to walk ahead of him to show him the road. He came forward instead and said: Walk behind me and direct me to the road, for we are a people who do not look upon the backs of women."

It is narrated from Ali that he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah when looking at women was mentioned, and he said: "The first glance is for you" — meaning the glance that falls unawares — "and the second is against you, and the third glance is a poisoned arrow from the arrows of Iblis. Whoever forsakes such glances for the sake of Allah Almighty, and for no other, Allah Almighty will requite him with a faith whose sweetness he will taste." And Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad said: "Do those who look upon the forms of women not fear that they may be afflicted with the like in their own wives?"

It is narrated from Ali that a man came to the Messenger of Allah and said: "O Messenger of Allah, should I ask my mother's leave before entering upon her?" He said: "Yes." The man asked: "And why, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Would it please you to see her unclothed?" The man said: "No." He said: "Then ask her leave." The man said: "O Messenger of Allah, my sister uncovers her hair before me." He said: "No." The man asked: "Why?" He said: "I fear that, should she reveal one of her charms before you, Satan may invite you toward her." And he said — upon him and his family be peace — "When one of you would kiss a woman who is a mahram to him and has come of age — a mother, a sister, an aunt, or any who is forbidden to him in marriage — let him kiss her upon the head and between the eyes, or let him refrain from her cheeks and her mouth."

Concerning Fatimah (ع): a blind man sought leave to enter upon her, and she veiled herself from him. It was said to her that he was blind — his sight wholly gone, unable to see anything of her. She said: "Even if he does not see me, I see him, and he perceives the voice and senses the scent."

The Messenger of Allah once posed a question to Ali and a company gathered before him: what is best for women? They did not know what to answer. Ali withdrew to Fatimah and put the question to her. She said: "What is best for women is that they should not see men and that men should not see them." Ali returned to the Messenger of Allah and reported this. He asked: "Did you arrive at this of yourself, or did another say it?" Ali said: "O Messenger of Allah, it was Fatimah who said it." The Messenger of Allah was pleased and said: "Fatimah is but a part of me."

### The Hunt and the Knife: Game, Slaughter, and Sacrifice

The Messenger of Allah taught that whoever desires to marry should not approach the matter heedlessly. He should begin by turning to Allah, praising Him and extolling Him, and then asking Him for the kind of companion that makes a household whole. He said that such a person should pray:

"O Allah, grant me a wife who is affectionate and fruitful, grateful and jealous in her honor. If I do good, she thanks me; if I do wrong, she forgives me; if I remember Allah, she helps me; if I forget, she reminds me; if I go out from her, she guards herself; if I come in to her, she gladdens me; if I command her, she obeys me; if I swear by her, she fulfills my oath; if she becomes angry, You satisfy me. O Lord of majesty and honor, grant me what I have asked for, and what You have apportioned and given."

A clear promise was attached to this supplication. The Messenger of Allah said that whoever recites these words and acts upon them, Allah Almighty will give him what he has asked.

He also taught that marriage is not to be entered without its proper preliminaries. The Messenger of Allah said that every marriage in which there is no engagement is like a leprous hand.

This same care for the right beginning was preserved by his descendants. When Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Ali gave a woman in marriage, or when a marriage was contracted in his presence, he would open with words of praise and testimony, saying: "Praise be to Allah. We praise Him and seek refuge with Him from the evils of ourselves and the evils of our deeds. Whoever Allah guides, none can mislead, and whoever He leaves to stray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger."

He would then recite the words of Allah Almighty:

﴿ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا وَنِسَاءً ۚ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسَاءَلُونَ بِهِ وَالْأَرْحَامَ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا ﴾

He would also recite the words of Allah Almighty:

﴿ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنتُم مُّسْلِمُونَ ﴾

Once the marriage has been thus commended and the standing of each party made known to the other, the contract is concluded. The one who performs it praises Allah for what He deserves, prays upon the Prophet ((ع) and his family), recalls the virtue of marriage and what is desired in it, and only then ties the knot. It is fitting that the husband make known to his prospective companion whatever he can of his circumstances, so that she enters the union in full awareness of his situation. If the contract is not preceded by a formal engagement, it remains permissible, though the khutbah is the better course.

The scholars forbade a formal proposal during the iddah, yet they permitted a discreet hint at marriage, in keeping with the words of Allah Almighty:

﴿ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا ۝ يُصْلِحْ لَكُمْ أَعْمَالَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ ۚ وَمَن يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ فَازَ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا ﴾

﴿ وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا عَرَّضْتُم بِهِ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ النِّسَاءِ أَوْ أَكْنَنتُمْ فِي أَنفُسِكُمْ ۚ عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ سَتَذْكُرُونَهُنَّ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا إِلَّا أَن تَقُولُوا قَوْلًا مَّعْرُوفًا ۚ وَلَا تَعْزِمُوا عُقْدَةَ النِّكَاحِ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ الْكِتَابُ أَجَلَهُ ﴾

*There is no blame upon you for what you hint at regarding a proposal to women, or what you conceal within yourselves. Allah knows that you will remember them, but do not make a secret commitment with them except in the form of honorable speech. And do not resolve the marriage contract until the prescribed term reaches its end.* (al-Baqarah: 235)

Jafar ibn Muhammad said concerning the words of Allah Almighty, "do not make a secret commitment with them": this refers to a secret pledge of marriage, while exposing them gently to the matter and speaking goodly words is the permitted hinting at the khutbah.

It is narrated that Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali visited Sakina bint Handhalah, who had recently been separated from a cousin of hers — a man who had married her and then died. Abu Jafar greeted her and said, "How have you been, O daughter of Handhalah?"

She said, "May I be your ransom, O son of the Messenger of Allah."

He said, "You know my kinship to the Messenger of Allah and his family, my standing with Ali, my right in Islam, and my honor among the Arabs."

She said, "May Allah forgive you, O Abu Jafar. You propose to me while I am in my iddah!"

He said, "I have done no such thing. I have only made known my status and my standing. The Messenger of Allah and his family once visited Umm Salamah, the daughter of Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumiyyah, while she was in her iddah from Abu Salamah, who was her cousin. He continued to speak of his standing to her until the impression of the mat showed upon his palm from the force with which he leaned upon his hand — and yet that was not a formal proposal."

The scholars held that it is recommended for one who wishes to marry to acquaint his prospective companion with his situation, so that she may come to know his circumstances.

It is related that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ and his family) proposed to her, Umm Salamah (رض) sent word to him saying, "O Messenger of Allah, I am an elderly woman, I have children, and I am a woman of great jealousy, and I fear there may be something in me of which you are unaware." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent back to her, "As for your age, you have mentioned it, and I am older than you. As for your children, they shall be among the children of the Messenger of Allah. And as for your jealousy, I shall pray to Allah Almighty to remove it from you." And he married her (ﷺ and his family).

**The Wedding Feast and the Consummation of Marriage**

The Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are reported to have taught that the wedding feast takes four forms:

- **The walimah** — the food prepared when a husband first enters upon his wife.
- **The khurs** — the food of the aqiqah, prepared for the newborn on the seventh day; its obligations have already been addressed.
- **The idhar** — the food prepared at the circumcision of a boy.
- **The wakirah** — the food a man prepares upon returning from a journey, to which he then invites people.

The Master (peace be upon him and his family) said that providing food at marriage is among the Sunnah of the Prophets. The Prophet ﷺ held a wedding feast for each of his wives upon consummating the marriage, and at some of those feasts he served al-hays — a food made of dates, ghee, and condensed milk. To one of his companions who had married, he said, "Give a feast, even if it be only with a sheep."

He also said (peace be upon him and his family), "The feast of the first day is a duty, the feast of the second day is a kindness known among people, and what lies beyond that is ostentation and reputation-seeking."

Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad (may the prayers of Allah be upon them) was once invited to a feast on the first day and accepted; he was invited again on the second day and accepted. When a messenger arrived on the third day to invite him, he ordered the messenger turned away until he had gone from sight.

It was narrated from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that he passed by Banu Zurayq and heard the sound of instruments and singing. He asked, "What is this?" They answered, "O Messenger of Allah, so-and-so has married so-and-so." He said, "He has completed his religion. This is marriage, not a clandestine affair — and there is no marriage in secret, until its smoke is seen and the sound of the tambourine is heard."

He also said (peace be upon him and his family), "What distinguishes marriage from fornication is the beating of the tambourine."

It was further narrated from him (peace be upon him and his family) that on the night Fatimah was brought to Ali, he heard the beat of the tambourine and asked, "What is this?" Umm Salamah said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is Asma bint Umays beating the tambourine for Fatimah, lest she say within herself, *My mother has died and there is no one to rejoice with me.*" The Messenger of Allah raised his hands toward the heavens and said, "O Allah, bring joy to Asma bint Umays as she has gladdened the daughter of Your Prophet." Then he called to her and said, "O Asma, what do you say when you beat the tambourine?" She replied, "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah I do not know what to say — I only wished to gladden her." He said, "Then say nothing indecent, but say: *We have come to you, we have come to you; so greet us and we will greet you.*"

Such speech, together with the beating of the tambourine and what resembles it, is what has been permitted at weddings and banquets. As for speech that carries vulgarity, the singing that accompanies it, and the instruments of diversion and the entrancing flutes that people of frivolity take up — those are disliked.

Al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad was asked about such things, and he recited the words of Allah Almighty:

﴿ وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاءَ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَاعِبِينَ ۝ لَوْ أَرَدْنَا أَن نَّتَّخِذَ لَهْوًا لَّاتَّخَذْنَاهُ مِن لَّدُنَّا إِن كُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ ۝ بَلْ نَقْذِفُ بِالْحَقِّ عَلَى الْبَاطِلِ فَيَدْمَغُهُ فَإِذَا هُوَ زَاهِقٌ ۚ وَلَكُمُ الْوَيْلُ مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ ﴾

It was narrated from him that he said, "Singing is a gathering upon which Allah Almighty does not look." It was also narrated that he was asked about the flute, and he said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: there are two voices that Allah Almighty detests — a wailing at the time of calamity, and a flute at the time of blessing." And it was narrated from him concerning the words of Allah Almighty:

﴿ فَاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الْأَوْثَانِ وَاجْتَنِبُوا قَوْلَ الزُّورِ ﴾

*So avoid the abomination of idols, and avoid the false statement* (al-Hajj: 30)

> وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشْتَرِى لَهْوَ ٱلْحَدِيثِ

that "the abomination of idols" includes chess, and that "the false statement" includes singing. He said further, concerning the words of Allah Almighty, ﴿ وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَن يَشْتَرِي لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ ﴾ *And among the people is he who purchases idle talk* (Luqman: 6), that this verse too refers to singing.

One of his companions reported: "I was in Madinah and came upon a place where singing was taking place, so I sat and listened. The following day I entered upon Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad, and when I had taken my seat before him, he opened by reciting the words of Allah, exalted be His mention:

﴿ إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُولَٰئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْئُولًا ﴾

*Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart: about all those one will be questioned.* (al-Isra: 36)

Then he looked at the companion and said, "You will be asked of your hearing what it heard, of your heart what it understood, and of your sight what it beheld."

It was also narrated from him that the sale of singing is not lawful, nor its purchase; that listening to it is hypocrisy, and teaching it is disbelief. It was further narrated that one day a delegation of his Shia arrived from various towns and entered upon him. He asked them, "Where have you lodged?" They said, "O son of the Messenger of Allah, we lodged in a house, and when we drew near to the place we heard singing within it, so we sought another lodging but could not find one." He said, "Even so, be noble: keep your hearing far from listening to it and lending it your ear, for Allah, exalted is the One who speaks, says:

﴿ وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ وَإِذَا مَرُّوا بِاللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا كِرَامًا ﴾

*And those who do not bear witness to falsehood, and when they pass by idle talk, they pass by with dignity.* (al-Furqan: 72)"

It was narrated from him that he said, "My father passed by me one day when I was a boy, and I had stopped to listen to two pipers. He took me by the hand and said, Step away; do not be of those who gloated over Adam (ع). I said, How is that, O my father? He said, All the amusement, play, and singing that you see was devised by Iblis to gloat over Adam when he was expelled from Paradise."

It was narrated from him that he said, "The house in which singing takes place is a house in which no calamity is met with comfort, no supplication is answered, and the angel does not enter."

It was narrated from him that he said, "Singing causes hypocrisy to grow in the heart as water causes the date palm to bring forth its spathe."

And it was narrated from him that he said, "Whoever has the lute played in his house for forty days, Allah sets over him a devil called al-Anqad, who leaves no limb of his without sitting upon it; and when he is thus afflicted, his sense of shame is stripped from him, and he no longer cares what he says or what is said to him."

> وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشْتَرِى لَهْوَ ٱلْحَدِيثِ

وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَن يَشْتَرِي لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ ﴾ *And among the people is he who purchases idle talk* (Luqman: 6). It was also narrated from him that singing bequeaths hypocrisy and brings on poverty.

It was reported to Jafar ibn Muhammad that a man of his Shia had visited an acquaintance, and that the host had brought out a slave-girl who played and sang before the guest. Jafar ibn Muhammad said, "Did he not fear that the command of Allah Almighty might come upon him in such a state — in a gathering upon which Allah does not look?"

It was also narrated from him that a man asked him about singing. He said to the man, "Tell me: when Allah Almighty separates truth from falsehood, where do you see singing falling?"

The man said, "O son of the Messenger of Allah, I see it only with falsehood."

He said, "Then you have judged it yourself. Leave it, for there is no good in it, and it is among those things for which Allah Almighty has promised the Fire." Then he recited the words of Allah Almighty: ﴿ وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَن يَشْتَرِي لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ ﴾ *And among the people is he who purchases idle talk* (Luqman: 6).

It was also narrated from him that singing bequeaths hypocrisy and brings on poverty.

The Master also related that the Messenger of Allah (ع and his family) forbade his community al-zafn, the flute, the drums, and the reed-pipes. He further related that a man who had broken a lute was once brought before Ali, and Ali approved his deed and ruled that no liability attached to the breaking of it.

All of this points to the prohibition of frivolity and of listening to singing, flutes, lyres, and the like when they are taken up for diversion. What is used in war, however — in the marshaling and parading of troops — stands apart. This includes what is raised before the Imams and the commanders of armies: the beating of drums and shields, and the blowing of horns and pipes not taken for enjoyment or amusement. Such things fall outside what has been forbidden and are, in their proper place, among what is recommended.

A narration from the Messenger of Allah (ع and his family) bears this out: he passed by a company of Abyssinians beating their drums, and he said, "Carry on, O sons of Arfidah, that the Jews may know there is breadth in our religion."

If someone should ask why, in the lands where the Imams hold authority (may the prayers of Allah be upon them), one hears and sees the very instruments of diversion they have forbidden, the answer is that this is no greater a problem than the indecencies Allah Almighty has forbidden and made unlawful, which people nonetheless commit behind their doors and curtains. Allah has commanded that the prescribed penalties be carried out for those indecencies upon which He has commanded such penalties — in what appears openly and is witnessed by witnesses. What remains hidden He alone, glorified be He, holds knowledge of, and He has reserved to Himself both its punishment and its pardon, advancing what He wills and deferring what He defers. It is well known and widely established among all people that the Imams denounced these things upon those who did them and withheld any license for them, holding that this is not a matter for which the hadd is due, but rather one calling for denunciation and prohibition.

It was narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ع and his family) that he said, "Bring your brides in by night, and give the feast by day." It was also narrated from him that he said, "There is no staying awake save in three: a vigil with the Quran, the seeking of knowledge, or the bringing of a bride to her husband." And it was narrated from him that a man should make himself ready for his wife as he would wish her to make herself ready for him. Jafar ibn Muhammad said that this means cleanliness.

When a man's wife is brought to him and she enters upon him, he should pray two rakahs, then place his hand upon her forelock and say, "O Allah, bless me in my wife and bless her in me; in whatever You have joined between us, join us in goodness, felicity, and blessing; and if You decree a parting, make it a parting toward every good." Then, when he sits beside her, he should wipe her forelock and say, "Praise be to Allah, who guided my straying, enriched my poverty, raised up my burden, gave might to my lowliness, sheltered my dependents, gave a spouse to my solitude, bore up my step, served my need, brought company to my loneliness, and lifted my standing; a praise wholesome, abundant, and blessed, for what You have granted, O Lord, and for what You have apportioned, and for what You have honored."

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali said that the woman too is commanded to be in a state of ablution on the night she is brought as a bride. When her husband prays, she prays; when he supplicates, she says amen. He further said that one should increase in supplication, sending prayers upon the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) at the beginning, the middle, and the end, and saying within it, "O Allah, grant me her affection, her warmth, her contentment with me and my contentment with her, and join us in the best of unions and the gentlest of bonds, for You love the lawful and hate the unlawful."

Jafar ibn Muhammad said that when a man wishes to come to his wife, he should say, "O Allah, if You decree from me this day a child, then make him purely Yours, and grant the devil no share in him, no portion and no part; indeed You are powerful over all things." It was narrated from the Messenger of Allah and his family that he said, "When one of you comes to his wife, let him not hasten her," and that when he is with her, he should deal kindly and truly with her. He and his family also forbade that a man be intimate with a free woman while another woman is present in the room. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali held that there is no harm in that with a bondwoman, and Jafar ibn Muhammad said the same. It was further narrated from Ali that he said it does not befit a man to be intimate with his wife

in the presence of another man. Jafar ibn Muhammad also said that when a man wishes to come to his wife, he should say: «اَللَّهُمَّ إِنْ قَضَيْتَ مِنِّي الْيَوْمَ خَلْقًا فَاجْعَلْهُ لَكَ خَالِصًا، وَلَا تَجْعَلْ لِلشَّيْطَانِ فِيهِ شِرْكًا وَلَا حَظًّا وَلَا نَصِيبًا، إِنَّكَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ» — "O Allah, if You decree from me today a creation, make it purely for You, and grant the devil in it no share, no portion, and no part, for You are able to do all things." It was also related from the Messenger of Allah and his family that he said: «إِذَا أَتَىٰ أَحَدُكُمُ امْرَأَتَهُ فَلَا يُعْجِلْهَا، وَإِذَا وَاقَعَهَا فَلْيَصْدُقْهَا» — "When one of you comes to his wife, let him not hasten her, and when he is with her, let him deal truthfully with her."

The Imams also permitted a man to come to a free wife while another wife was present in the house. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him, held that there was no objection to this in the case of a bondwoman, and Jafar ibn Muhammad said the same. From Ali it was related that a man should not come to his wife while facing the qibla. He further said that gazing during intercourse brings on blindness. The Prophet, his family, and the Imams of his progeny would turn their faces away whenever an animal was being mounted upon the road.

He named a hidden form of infanticide — الْوَأْدُ الْخَفِيُّ: a man comes to a woman, and when he senses the issuing of the fluid, he withdraws and spills it elsewhere. Of this he said, "So do not do that." He also said that the Messenger of Allah, and his family, forbade withdrawal from a free woman except with her leave, and from a bondwoman taken in marriage except with the leave of her master. Ali said that a man may withdraw from his own bondwoman as he wishes, and Jafar ibn Muhammad said the same.

From Ali by way of Jafar ibn Muhammad: a man should not lie between two free women, though he may lie between two bondwomen. He should not look upon the awrah of a free woman, nor expose his own awrah to her.

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali said that intercourse is disliked at the following times:

- From the breaking of dawn until sunrise, and from the setting of the sun until the fading of twilight
- On the night in which the moon is eclipsed, and on the day in which the sun is eclipsed
- On the day and night in which the earth quakes
- When the yellow, the black, and the red winds blow

He said: The Messenger of Allah and his family spent a night with one of his wives on a night in which the moon was eclipsed, and nothing passed between them. It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is this coldness?" He said, "It is no coldness, but this was a sign, and I was loath to take my pleasure on such a night, that I might not be among those whom Allah, mighty and majestic, has rebuked in His Book where He says: «وَإِن يَرَوْا كِسْفًا مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ سَاقِطًا يَقُولُوا سَحَابٌ مَّرْكُومٌ» And were they to see a fragment falling from the sky, they would say: a heaped-up cloud."

Then Abu Jafar, may Allah's blessings be upon him, said: By Him who sent Muhammad with prophethood, singled him out with the message, and honored him with nobility, none of you comes to his wife at any of these disliked times and is then granted offspring in whom he sees the delight of his eye.

From Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him: a slave girl under nine years of age is not to be approached; if a man does so and she is harmed, he is liable. Jafar ibn Muhammad, may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family, said that if a man marries a young girl, he does not enter upon her until she has completed nine years from the day of her birth.

It was also related from Ali, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he disliked approaching women in their hinder parts and used to forbid it, citing the words of Allah, mighty and majestic, that one may come to them only «فِي الْفُرُوجِ مِنْ قُبُلٍ أَوْ دُبُرٍ» — in the place of tilth, whether from before or from behind. And from the Messenger of Allah and his family, it was related that he said: «لَا يَخْلُو رَجُلٌ بِامْرَأَةٍ غَيْرِ ذَاتِ مَحْرَمٍ مِنْهُ إِلَّا كَانَ الشَّيْطَانُ ثَالِثَهُمَا» "No man is alone with a woman who is not his mahram but that the devil is the third of them." He forbade conversing with women other than one's wives and one's mahrams.

Jafar ibn Muhammad, may Allah's blessings be upon him, said: «حَدِيثُ النِّسَاءِ يُورِثُ النِّسْيَانَ وَيُزِيغُ الْقَلْبَ وَهُوَ مِنْ مَصَائِدِ الشَّيْطَانِ» "Idle talk with women breeds forgetfulness and makes the heart swerve, and it is among the snares of the devil."

> فَإِن طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَن شَىْءٍۢ مِّنْهُ

The Messenger of Allah, upon him and his family be peace, said: «اِتَّقُوا اللَّهَ فِي النِّسَاءِ، فَإِنَّهُنَّ عِيٌّ وَعَوْرَةٌ، وَإِنَّكُمُ اسْتَحْلَلْتُمُوهُنَّ بِأَمَانَةِ اللَّهِ» "Fear Allah concerning women, for they are weak of speech and are a thing to be covered, and you have made them lawful to you by the trust of Allah."

He said: their weakness calls for restraint in speech toward them, and what is to be covered must be sheltered within the home. They are not to be lodged in upper rooms, not to be taught writing — but they are to be taught Surat al-Nur.

From him, upon him and his family be peace, it is also related: «نِعْمَ شُغْلُ الْمَرْأَةِ الْمُؤْمِنَةِ الْمِغْزَلُ» "How excellent an occupation for a believing woman is the spindle."

And from him likewise: when he took the pledge from women, he required of them that they would not speak with men other than their husbands and their mahrams.

It was also related that he forbade women to look upon men, and that a woman should not leave her house without her husband's leave — not even for the bath, save out of necessity. And it was related that one day he said to his companions, "What is the woman?" They said, "An awrah, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "Yes." Then he asked, "And when is she nearest to her Lord?" They had no answer to give. Ali mentioned this to Fatimah, may Allah's blessings be upon her, and she said, "Return to him and say: O Messenger of Allah, the nearest a woman is to her Lord is when she keeps to the innermost of her house." He went and informed the Prophet and his family, who said, "This is from you, O Ali." He replied, "No, O Messenger of Allah, rather it was Fatimah who said it." The Messenger of Allah, upon him and his family be peace, said, "She has spoken truly; «إِنَّهَا بِضْعَةٌ مِنِّي» indeed she is a part of me."

From the Messenger of Allah and his family: he forbade a woman to walk unclothed before her husband, and forbade a man to be unclothed before her. He forbade women to dress their hair with wine or to apply its dregs. He forbade women to imitate men and men to imitate women, and he cursed whoever did so. From him: "Any woman who perfumes herself, let her not leave her house, nor attend the prayer with us." From him also: he forbade women, when walking behind men, to take the middle of the road alongside them, and he said, "Women have no portion of the middle of the road." He forbade a woman, when going out, to wear a garment that draws notice, to adorn herself with anything that makes a sound, or to strike her foot so that the chime of her anklet is heard. He forbade women from open display, from wailing, and from raising the voice except out of necessity — and from conversing freely with men, and from spending the night away from their homes.

He forbade the giving of greeting to women. He also said that a man should not touch another man unless there is a garment between them, nor a woman another woman unless there is a garment between them.

A woman came to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have a husband who is harsh of nature, and I have worked something to turn his affection toward me." The Messenger of Allah said to her, "Fie upon you! You have sullied your religion, and the angels of heaven and the angels of earth have cursed you."

He also said: «لَوْ كُنْتُ آمِرًا أَحَدًا أَنْ يَسْجُدَ لِأَحَدٍ لَأَمَرْتُ الْمَرْأَةَ أَنْ تَسْجُدَ لِزَوْجِهَا» — "Had I been commanding anyone to prostrate to another, I would have commanded the woman to prostrate to her husband."

He forbade a woman to deny her husband herself when he called her, and to deny him her help and her work. He said, "The best thing with which a woman adorns herself is the fear of Allah and obedience to her husband."

When a woman knows her Lord, believes in Him and in His Messenger, acknowledges the merit of the People of the House of her Prophet, performs the five prayers, fasts the month of Ramadan, guards her chastity, and obeys her husband, she may enter Paradise by whichever of its gates she wishes.

A woman once sent word to him saying, "O Messenger of Allah, my husband has ordered me not to go out, near or far, until he returns from his journey; and my father is in the market. Shall I go out to him?" The Messenger of Allah said to her, "Sit in your house and obey your husband." She did so, and her father died. The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, then sent word to her saying, "Truly Allah, mighty and majestic, has forgiven your father on account of your obedience to your husband."

A woman put a question to him, may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of the husband over the wife?"

He said, "She must not give in charity from his house except by his leave, nor deny him herself even upon the saddle's back, nor fast a voluntary day except by his leave, nor leave her house except by his leave. And if she goes out without his leave, the angels of heaven, the angels of earth, the angels of mercy, and the angels of wrath curse her until she returns."

She said, "O Messenger of Allah, who has the greatest right over a man?"

He said, "His parents."

"And who has the greatest right over a woman?"

He said, "Her husband."

She said, "O Messenger of Allah, then have I no right over him to match what he has over me?"

He said, "No, not even one in a hundred."

It was also related that he assigned to his daughter Fatimah, may Allah's blessings be upon her, responsibility for the affairs within the house, and assigned to Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him, responsibility for the affairs outside it.
